passages.ctx: From the Sermon on the Mount.
passages.en: Blessed are the merciful, because they themselves will be shown mercy.

rows.note: μακάριοι: blessed, from μακάριος. Greek needs no word for are. Latin: beātī, from beātus.
οἱ ἐλεήμονες: the merciful. οἱ is the plural of ὁ, the. Latin has no such word: misericordēs.
ὅτι: because. Latin: quoniam.
αὐτοί: they, from αὐτός. The verb already means they, so this adds weight: they themselves. Latin: ipsī, from ipse.
ἐλεηθήσονται: they will be shown mercy, a future passive. Latin needs two words: misericordiam cōnsequentur, they will obtain mercy, from misericordia and cōnsequor.

passages.ctx: Jesus sends out the twelve apostles.
passages.en: The one welcoming you welcomes me, and the one welcoming me welcomes the one who sent me.

rows.note: ὁ: the, here with a participle, so the one who. Latin uses quī, who.
δεχόμενος: welcoming, a present participle of δέχομαι, to receive or welcome. Its endings look passive, but the meaning is active. Latin uses a plain verb, recipit, from recipiō.
ὑμᾶς: you, plural, from σύ, you. Latin: vōs, also plural.
ἐμέ: me, from ἐγώ, I. It comes first for emphasis. Latin: mē, from ego.
δέχεται: he welcomes, the plain present. Latin again: recipit.
καί: and, one of the most common Greek words. Latin: et.
ὁ: the one who. quī.
ἐμέ, mē.
δεχόμενος: welcoming. Latin, recipit.
δέχεται, recipit.
τόν: the, in the accusative. Latin has no article, so it says eum, him, from is.
ἀποστείλαντα: having sent, an aorist participle of ἀποστέλλω, to send out. Latin makes a clause: quī mē mīsit, who sent me, from mittō.
με: me, the short unstressed form. Latin: mē.

ng.m: I, me; pl. ἡμεῖς we, us

passages.ctx: Jesus answers those who say he drives out demons by Beelzebul.
passages.en: The one who is not with me is against me, and the one who does not gather with me scatters.

rows.note: ὁ: the. With a participle it means the one who. Latin uses quī, who.
μὴ: not. Greek has two words for not, and μή goes with participles. Latin: nōn.
ὢν: being, the present participle of εἰμί, to be. Latin has no such participle, so it says est, is, from sum.
μετ’ ἐμοῦ: with me. μετά, with, drops its last vowel before a vowel. ἐμοῦ is the genitive of ἐγώ, I. Latin joins them: mēcum.
κατ’ ἐμοῦ: against me. κατά with the genitive means against. Latin: contrā mē.
ἐστιν: is. Latin again: est.
καί: and. Latin: et.
ὁ μὴ: again, the one who does not. Latin: quī nōn.
συνάγων: gathering, the present participle of συνάγω, to gather together. Latin uses a plain verb: congregat, he gathers, from congregō.
μετ’ ἐμοῦ, mēcum.
σκορπίζει: he scatters, from σκορπίζω. Latin: spargit, from spargō.

passages.ctx: Jesus begins to explain the parable of the sower to his disciples.
passages.en: You, then, listen to the parable of the sower.

rows.note: ὑμεῖς: you, plural, from σύ, you. The verb already says you, so this is emphatic. Latin: vōs.
οὖν: then, so, drawing a conclusion. It comes second in its clause. Latin: ergō, therefore.
ἀκούσατε: listen, from ἀκούω, to hear. It is an aorist command, spoken to many. Latin: audīte, from audiō.
τὴν παραβολὴν: the parable, from παραβολή. The accusative marks the object. Latin borrows the word: parabolam.
τοῦ σπείραντος: of the sower, literally of the one who sowed, an aorist participle of σπείρω, to sow. Latin has a present participle, of the one sowing: sēminantis, from sēminō.

passages.ctx: In the parable, a vineyard owner answers a worker who grumbles about his pay.
passages.en: But he, answering one of them, said, ‘Friend, I am not wronging you. Was it not for a denarius that you agreed with me?’

rows.note: ὁ, standing alone as he. Latin: ille, that one.
δὲ: but. It comes second in its clause. Latin: at.
ἀποκριθεὶς: answering, from ἀποκρίνομαι. Passive in form, active in meaning. Latin: respondēns, from respondeō.
ἑνὶ: to one, from εἷς. Latin: ūnī, from ūnus.
αὐτῶν: of them. Latin: eōrum, from is.
εἶπεν: he said, the aorist of λέγω, to say. Latin: dīxit, from dīcō.
ἑταῖρε: friend, a vocative, used to address someone. Latin: amīce.
οὐκ: not, from οὐ, written οὐκ before a vowel. Latin: nōn.
ἀδικῶ: I wrong, from ἀδικέω. Latin uses a phrase: faciō injūriam, I do injury, from faciō, to do or make.
σε: you. Latin has the dative: tibi, to you, from tū.
οὐχὶ: not, a stronger οὐ. It opens a question expecting yes. So does the Latin nōnne.
δηναρίου: for a denarius, a day of wages. The genitive gives the price. Latin: ex dēnāriō, using ex, out of.
συνεφώνησάς: you agreed, from συμφωνέω. Latin: convēnistī, you came together, from conveniō.
μοι: with me. Latin: mēcum.

passages.ctx: In the parable of the wedding feast, a guest has no wedding garment.
passages.en: Then the king said to the servants, ‘Tie his feet and hands, and throw him out into the darkness outside. There will be the weeping and the grinding of teeth.’

rows.note: τότε: then, at that time. Latin: tunc.
ὁ βασιλεὺς: the king, from βασιλεύς. Latin has no word for the: rēx.
εἶπεν: he said, from λέγω. Latin has the present, dīcit, he says, which tells the story vividly.
τοῖς διακόνοις: to the servants, from διάκονος, servant. The dative means to. Latin: ministrīs, from minister.
δήσαντες: having tied, an aorist participle of δέω, to bind. Latin turns it around with an ablative absolute, a phrase set apart in the ablative: ligātīs, having been tied, from ligō.
αὐτοῦ: his. Latin, ejus, placed after the nouns.
πόδας: feet, the accusative plural of πούς, foot. Latin: pedibus, from pēs. Latin names the hands first.
καὶ, et.
χεῖρας: hands, from χείρ, hand. Latin: manibus, from manus.
ἐκβάλετε: throw out, an aorist command from ἐκβάλλω, made of ἐκ, out, and βάλλω, to throw. Latin: mittite, send, from mittō.
αὐτὸν: him. Latin, eum.
εἰς: into, with the accusative. Latin: in, which means into when it takes the accusative.
τὸ σκότος: the darkness, from σκότος, a neuter noun. Latin uses a plural word: tenebrās, from tenebrae, darkness.
τὸ ἐξώτερον: the outer, a comparative, from ἐξώτερος, farther out. Greek repeats the article. Latin: exteriōrēs, from exterior.
ἐκεῖ: there. Latin: ibi.
ἔσται: will be, the future of εἰμί. Latin: erit.
ὁ κλαυθμὸς: the weeping, from κλαυθμός. Latin: flētus, a noun from fleō, to weep.
καὶ, et.
ὁ βρυγμὸς: the grinding, from βρυγμός. Latin: strīdor, a harsh grating sound.
τῶν ὀδόντων: of the teeth, the genitive plural of ὀδούς, tooth. Latin: dentium, from dēns.

nl.m: in, on (+ abl.); into, onto, against (+acc.)

passages.ctx: Jesus speaks against the scribes and Pharisees.
passages.en: But woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites, because you lock the kingdom of the heavens in front of people; for you are not going in, nor do you let those who are going in enter.

rows.note: οὐαὶ: woe, a cry of grief and warning. Latin: vae.
δὲ: but. Latin: autem, but, which like δέ comes second in its clause.
ὑμῖν: to you, the dative plural of σύ. Latin: vōbīs.
γραμματεῖς: scribes, from γραμματεύς, a scribe, an expert in the law. It is vocative, addressing them. Latin: scrībae, from scrība.
καὶ, et.
Φαρισαῖοι: Pharisees. Latin: Pharisaeī, from Pharisaeus.
ὑποκριταί: hypocrites, from ὑποκριτής, which first meant an actor on the stage. Latin simply borrows it: hypocritae.
ὅτι: because. Latin: quia.
κλείετε: you lock, from κλείω, to shut. Latin: clauditis, from claudō.
τὴν βασιλείαν: the kingdom, from βασιλεία, kingdom or reign, akin to βασιλεύς, king. Latin: rēgnum.
τῶν οὐρανῶν: of the heavens, the genitive plural of οὐρανός, heaven or sky. Latin keeps the plural: caelōrum, from caelum.
ἔμπροσθεν: in front of, with the genitive. Latin: ante, before.
τῶν ἀνθρώπων: people, from ἄνθρωπος, a human being. Latin: hominēs, from homō, in the accusative after ante.
ὑμεῖς: you, stated for emphasis. Latin: vōs.
γὰρ: for, giving a reason. Like δέ, it comes second. So does the Latin enim.
οὐκ: not. Latin: nōn.
εἰσέρχεσθε: you go in, from εἰσέρχομαι, to enter: εἰς, into, and ἔρχομαι, to come or go. The form is middle, but the meaning is active. Latin: intrātis, from intrō.
οὐδὲ: nor, made of οὐ and δέ. Latin: nec.
τοὺς εἰσερχομένους: those going in, a present participle with the article. Latin: introeuntēs, from introeō, to go in.
ἀφίετε: you let, from ἀφίημι, to let go or permit, and also to forgive. Latin: sinitis, from sinō, to allow.
εἰσελθεῖν: to enter, the aorist infinitive. Latin: intrāre.

nl.m: and not, nor; nec … nec neither … nor

passages.ctx: Jesus teaches in the synagogue at Capernaum.
passages.en: And they were astounded at his teaching, for he was teaching them like someone who has authority, and not like the scribes.

rows.note: καὶ, et.
ἐξεπλήσσοντο: they were astounded, from ἐκπλήσσομαι, to be struck with amazement. It is imperfect, an ongoing past. Latin: stupēbant, also imperfect, from stupeō.
ἐπὶ: on, upon, here at, from ἐπί. Latin: super, over, here with the ablative.
τῇ διδαχῇ: the teaching, from διδαχή, in the dative. Latin: doctrīnā, from doctrīna.
αὐτοῦ: his. Latin, ejus.
ἦν: he was, the imperfect of εἰμί. Latin: erat.
γὰρ: for. Latin: enim.
διδάσκων: teaching, the present participle of διδάσκω, to teach. With ἦν it makes was teaching, and Latin copies this: erat docēns, from doceō.
αὐτοὺς: them. Latin, eōs.
ὡς: as, like. Latin: quasi, as if.
ἐξουσίαν: authority, from ἐξουσία, the right or power to act. Latin: potestātem, from potestās.
ἔχων: having, the present participle of ἔχω, to have. Latin: habēns, from habeō.
καὶ, et.
οὐχ: not, spelled with chi before a rough breathing. Latin: nōn.
ὡς again. This time Latin says sīcut, just as.
οἱ γραμματεῖς: the scribes. Latin: scrībae.

nl.m: over, upon, above (+ acc.); about (+ abl.)
as if, as it were; about (with numbers)
just as, as; as it were

passages.ctx: Jesus leaves the synagogue at Capernaum with his first disciples.
passages.en: And at once, coming out of the synagogue, they went into the house of Simon and Andrew with James and John.

rows.note: καὶ, et.
εὐθὺς: at once, from εὐθύς, straight or immediate. Mark uses it again and again. Latin: prōtinus, straightway.
ἐκ: out of, with the genitive. Latin: dē, down from, out of.
τῆς συναγωγῆς: the synagogue, from συναγωγή, a gathering, related to συνάγω, to gather. Latin borrows it: synagōgā.
ἐξελθόντες: having come out, an aorist participle of ἐξέρχομαι, to go out. Latin uses a present participle, going out: ēgredientēs, from ēgredior.
ἦλθον: they went, the aorist of ἔρχομαι, to come or go. Latin: vēnērunt, they came, the perfect of veniō.
εἰς: into. Latin: in.
τὴν οἰκίαν: the house, from οἰκία. Latin: domum, from domus.
Σίμωνος: of Simon, the genitive. Latin: Simōnis.
καὶ, et.
Ἀνδρέου: of Andrew. Latin: Andreae.
μετὰ: with. Latin: cum, with, taking the ablative.
Ἰακώβου: James, in the genitive. It is the name behind English James. Latin: Jacōbō, in the ablative.
καὶ, et.
Ἰωάννου: John. Latin: Jōanne.

nl.m: from, down from, out of; about, concerning

passages.ctx: Jesus is teaching in a crowded house in Capernaum.
passages.en: And they come, bringing a paralysed man to him, carried by four.

rows.note: καὶ, et.
ἔρχονται: they come, a vivid present. Latin uses the perfect: vēnērunt, they came.
φέροντες: bringing, from φέρω, to carry. Latin has the same root: ferentēs, from ferō.
πρὸς: to, toward. Latin: ad.
αὐτὸν: him. Latin, eum.
παραλυτικὸν: a paralysed man. Latin borrows it: paralyticum.
αἰρόμενον: being carried, a present passive participle of αἴρω, to lift or carry. Latin uses a clause: quī portābātur, who was being carried.
ὑπὸ: by, with the genitive. Latin: ā, with the ablative.
τεσσάρων: four. Latin: quatuor, which never changes its ending.

nl.m: to, toward; at, near;for, in order to

passages.ctx: The disciples have asked Jesus about the parable of the sower.
passages.en: And he says to them, ‘You do not know this parable? And how will you come to know all the parables?’

rows.note: καὶ, et.
λέγει: he says, the present of λέγω. Latin: ait, from aiō, a common verb of saying.
αὐτοῖς: to them, dative plural. Latin: illīs, from ille.
οὐκ οἴδατε: you do not know. οἴδατε is from οἶδα, to know, a perfect in form but present in meaning. Latin uses one word: nescītis, from nesciō, not to know.
τὴν παραβολὴν: the parable. Latin: parabolam.
ταύτην: this, from οὗτος, this one. Greek puts it after the noun and its article. Latin: hanc, from hic.
καὶ, et.
πῶς: how. Latin: quōmodo, in what way.
πάσας: all, a feminine plural of πᾶς, all or every. Latin: omnēs, from omnis.
τὰς παραβολὰς: the parables, now plural. Latin: parabolās.
γνώσεσθε: you will know, the future of γινώσκω, to know or come to know. Its future is middle in form. Latin: cognōscētis, from cognōscō.

nl.m: all, every, whole; pl. all, everyone

passages.ctx: The local people have seen Jesus heal a man possessed by demons.
passages.en: And they began to plead with him to go away from their district.

rows.note: καὶ, et.
ἤρξαντο: they began, from ἄρχω, which in the middle voice means to begin. Latin: coepērunt, from coepī.
παρακαλεῖν: to plead with, from παρακαλέω, to urge or comfort. Latin: rogāre, to ask, from rogō.
αὐτὸν: him. Latin, eum.
ἀπελθεῖν: to go away, the aorist infinitive of ἀπέρχομαι, made from ἀπό, away, and ἔρχομαι. Latin uses a clause: ut discēderet, that he should depart, from ut, that, and discēdō.
ἀπὸ: from, away from, with the genitive. Latin: dē.
τῶν ὁρίων: the district, literally the boundaries, from ὅριον. Latin: fīnibus, from fīnis, border.
αὐτῶν: their. Latin, eōrum.

nl.m: that, so that, in order that; as, when

passages.ctx: A woman who had bled for twelve years touches Jesus’ cloak.
passages.en: And at once the source of her bleeding dried up, and she knew in her body that she had been healed of the affliction.

rows.note: καί, et.
εὐθύς: at once. Latin, cōnfestim.
ἐξηράνθη: dried up, from ξηραίνω. Latin: siccātus est, from siccō.
ἡ πηγή: the source, a spring. Latin: fōns.
τοῦ αἵματος: of the blood, the genitive of αἷμα, blood. Latin: sanguinis, from sanguis.
αὐτῆς: her. Latin, ejus.
καί, et.
ἔγνω: she knew, from γινώσκω. Latin: sēnsit, she felt, from sentiō.
τῷ σώματι: in the body, from σῶμα. A plain dative. Latin: corpore, a plain ablative, from corpus.
ὅτι: that. Latin, quia.
ἴαται: she has been healed, a perfect of ἰάομαι, to heal. Latin: sānāta esset, had been healed, from sānō.
ἀπὸ τῆς μάστιγος: from the affliction. μάστιξ means a whip, then a torment. Latin: ā plāgā, from a blow.

passages.en: And at once Jesus, recognizing within himself the power that had gone out from him, turning around in the crowd, kept saying, “Who touched my clothes?”

rows.note: καί, et.
εὐθύς: at once. Latin now says statim, immediately.
ὁ Ἰησοῦς: Jesus, with the article. Latin: Jēsūs.
ἐπιγνούς: recognizing, from ἐπιγινώσκω, to know fully. An aorist participle. Latin: cognōscēns, from cognōscō.
ἐν: in, followed by the dative. Latin: in.
ἑαυτῷ: himself, from ἑαυτοῦ, the reflexive pronoun. Latin: sēmetipsō, an emphatic form of sē.
τὴν δύναμιν: the power, from δύναμις, power, might. Latin: virtūtem, from virtūs, strength.
ἐξ αὐτοῦ: out of him, set between article and noun. Latin: dē illō.
ἐξελθοῦσαν: gone out, a participle of ἐξέρχομαι. Latin uses a clause: quae exierat, which had gone out, from exeō.
ἐπιστραφείς: turning around, from ἐπιστρέφω. Latin: conversus, from convertō. Both are passive in form.
ἐν τῷ ὄχλῳ: in the crowd, from ὄχλος, crowd. Latin says ad turbam, toward the crowd, from turba.
ἔλεγεν: he was saying, an imperfect. Latin: aiēbat, also imperfect.
τίς: who, the question word. Latin: quis.
μου: my, literally of me, placed before the verb. Latin: mea, from meus.
ἥψατο: touched, from ἅπτω. In the middle voice it means to touch, and it takes the genitive. Latin: tetigit, from tangō, with an accusative.
τῶν ἱματίων: the clothes, from ἱμάτιον, garment, cloak. Genitive after the verb of touching. Latin: vestīmenta, from vestīmentum.

passages.ctx: Jesus has sent his disciples across the lake and stayed behind to pray.
passages.en: And as evening fell, the boat was in the middle of the sea, and he himself was alone on land.

rows.note: καί, et.
ὀψίας: evening, from ὀψία. Latin: sērō, late, an adverb.

γενομένης: having come, from γίνομαι, to become, to happen. With ὀψίας it makes a genitive absolute, a small time clause: evening having come. Latin uses cum with a subjunctive: cum sērō esset, when it was late.
ἦν: was. Latin, erat.
τὸ πλοῖον: the boat. Latin: nāvis, ship or boat.
ἐν: in. Latin, in.
μέσῳ: the middle, from μέσος, middle, a dative after ἐν. Latin: mediō, from medius.
τῆς θαλάσσης: of the sea, from θάλασσα, sea. Latin: marī, from mare. Latin makes middle an adjective agreeing with sea: in mediō marī, in mid sea.
καί, et.
αὐτός: he himself. Latin, ipse.
μόνος: alone, only. Greek needs no verb here. Latin: sōlus.
ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς: on the land, from γῆ, earth, land. ἐπί with the genitive means on. Latin: in terrā, from terra.

passages.ctx: Jesus speaks about what makes a person unclean.
passages.en: And calling the crowd to him again, he was saying to them, “Hear me, every one of you, and understand.”

rows.note: καί, et.
προσκαλεσάμενος: having called them to himself, an aorist participle of προσκαλέομαι, to summon. Latin: advocāns, calling.
πάλιν: again. Latin: iterum.
τὸν ὄχλον: the crowd. Latin: turbam.
ἔλεγεν: he was saying. Latin: dīcēbat.
αὐτοῖς: to them. Latin: illīs.
ἀκούσατέ μου: hear me. The verb ἀκούω takes the genitive, μου, of me. Latin uses the accusative: audīte mē.
πάντες: all. Latin: omnēs.
καί, et.
σύνετε: understand. A command, from συνίημι. Latin: intelligite, from intellegō, to understand.

passages.ctx: A hungry crowd has followed Jesus into a deserted place.
passages.en: And he was asking them, “How many loaves do you have?” And they said, “Seven.”

rows.note: καί, et.
ἠρώτα: he was asking, from ἐρωτάω, to ask. An imperfect, an action in progress. Latin uses the perfect: interrogāvit, from interrogō.
αὐτούς: them. Latin, eōs.
πόσους: how many, from πόσος. Latin: quot, which never changes its ending.
ἔχετε: you have, plural. Latin: habētis.
ἄρτους: loaves, from ἄρτος, bread, a loaf. Latin: pānēs, from pānis.
οἱ δέ: and they. The article with δέ marks a change of speaker. Latin: quī, who, linking back.
εἶπαν: they said. Latin, dīxērunt.
ἑπτά: seven. Latin: septem. Neither changes its ending, and the two share an ancient root.

passages.ctx: Jesus has just fed four thousand people.
passages.en: And at once, boarding the boat with his disciples, he went into the regions of Dalmanutha.

rows.note: καί, et.
εὐθύς, statim: at once.
ἐμβάς: stepping in, from ἐμβαίνω, to embark. Latin: ascendēns, going up, from ascendō.
εἰς τὸ πλοῖον: into the boat. Latin drops the preposition: nāvim, the accusative of nāvis.
μετὰ τῶν μαθητῶν: with the disciples, from μαθητής, disciple, learner. Latin: cum discipulīs, from discipulus.
αὐτοῦ: his. Latin: suīs, from suus, his own, pointing back to the subject.
ἦλθεν: he went. Latin: vēnit, a perfect, with a long e.
εἰς τὰ μέρη: into the regions, from μέρος, part, region. Latin: in partēs, from pars, also part.
Δαλμανουθά: Dalmanutha, a place name found only here. Latin keeps it: Dalmanūtha.

passages.ctx: Jesus ends a parable about tenants who killed the owner’s son.
passages.en: Have you not even read this scripture: ‘A stone which the builders rejected, this one became the head of the corner; from the Lord this came about, and it is wonderful in our eyes’?

rows.note: οὐδέ: not even. Latin: nec.
τὴν γραφήν: the scripture, from γραφή, a writing. Latin: scrīptūram, from scrīptūra.
ταύτην: this, from οὗτος. Latin: hanc, from hic.
ἀνέγνωτε: you read, plural, from ἀναγινώσκω. Latin: lēgistis, from legō.
λίθον: stone, from λίθος, accusative by attraction to the relative after it. Latin follows: lapidem, from lapis.
ὅν: which, from ὅς, the relative pronoun. Latin: quem, from quī.
ἀπεδοκίμασαν: they rejected, from ἀποδοκιμάζω, to reject after testing. Latin: reprobāvērunt.
οἱ οἰκοδομοῦντες: the builders, literally those building, from οἰκοδομέω. Latin also uses a participle: aedificantēs.
οὗτος: this one. Latin: hic.
ἐγενήθη: became, an aorist passive form of γίνομαι. Latin: factus est, from fīō, to become.
εἰς κεφαλήν: into a head, from κεφαλή. εἰς marks what something becomes. Latin copies it: in caput.
γωνίας: of the corner, from γωνία. Latin: angulī, from angulus.
παρά: from, with the genitive. Latin: ā.
κυρίου: the Lord, from κύριος, lord, master. Latin: Dominō, from dominus.
ἐγένετο: it came about, the same verb. Latin: factum est, neuter.
αὕτη: this, feminine, copying a Hebrew idiom. Latin makes it neuter: istud, from iste.
καί, et.
ἔστιν: it is. Latin, est.
θαυμαστή: wonderful, from θαυμαστός, feminine. Latin: mīrābile, neuter, from mīrābilis.
ἐν: in. Latin, in.
ὀφθαλμοῖς: eyes, from ὀφθαλμός. Latin: oculīs, from oculus.
ἡμῶν: our, literally of us. Latin uses an adjective, nostrīs, from noster.

nl.m: become; be made, be done; happen

passages.ctx: Jesus tells his disciples about the troubles to come.
passages.en: And to all the nations the good news must first be proclaimed.

rows.note: καί, et.
εἰς: to, into. Latin: in, with the accusative.
πάντα: all, from πᾶς, neuter to match nations. Latin: omnēs, from omnis.
τὰ ἔθνη: the nations, from ἔθνος, nation, people. In the plural it often means the Gentiles. Latin: gentēs, from gēns.
πρῶτον: first, from πρῶτος, the neuter used as an adverb. Latin does the same: prīmum, from prīmus.
δεῖ: it is necessary, must. It has no personal subject and takes an infinitive. Latin oportet works the same way.
κηρυχθῆναι: to be proclaimed, from κηρύσσω, to proclaim like a herald. An aorist passive infinitive. Latin: praedicārī, the passive infinitive of praedicō.
τὸ εὐαγγέλιον: the good news. It is the subject of the infinitive. Latin simply borrows the Greek word: Ēvangelium.

nl.m: it is necessary, one must, ought

passages.en: And Judas Iscariot, the one from the twelve, went away to the chief priests so that he might hand him over to them.

rows.note: καί, et.
Ἰούδας: Judas, the Greek form of Judah. Latin: Jūdās.
Ἰσκαριώθ: Iscariot, which does not decline. Latin: Iscariōtēs, which does.
ὁ εἷς: the one. Latin: ūnus, with no article.
τῶν δώδεκα: of the twelve, from δώδεκα, which never changes. Latin: dē duodecim, from the twelve.
ἀπῆλθεν: he went away, from ἀπέρχομαι. Latin: abiit, from abeō, to go away.
πρός: to. Latin, ad.
τοὺς ἀρχιερεῖς: the chief priests, from ἀρχιερεύς, high priest. Latin takes two words: summōs sacerdōtēs, highest priests, from sacerdōs, priest.
ἵνα: so that, introducing a purpose. Its verb goes into the subjunctive. Latin: ut, which does the same.
αὐτόν: him. Latin, eum.
παραδοῖ: he might hand over, from παραδίδωμι, to hand over, betray. An aorist subjunctive. Latin: prōderet, from prōdō, to betray.
αὐτοῖς: to them, the dative. Latin: illīs.

ng.m: so that, in order that; that

passages.ctx: At the Last Supper.
passages.en: And taking a cup and giving thanks, he gave it to them, and all of them drank from it.

rows.note: καί, et.
λαβών: taking, from λαμβάνω, to take, to receive. An aorist participle. Latin: acceptō calice, an ablative absolute, the cup having been taken, from accipiō.
ποτήριον: a cup. Latin: calice, from calix.
εὐχαριστήσας: giving thanks, from εὐχαριστέω. Latin needs two words: grātiās agēns, from grātia, thanks, and agō, to do.
ἔδωκεν: he gave, from δίδωμι, to give, an aorist. Latin: dedit, from dō, to give, a perfect. The two are related.
αὐτοῖς: to them. Latin, eīs.
καί, et.
ἔπιον: they drank, from πίνω, to drink, an aorist. Latin: bibērunt, from bibō.
ἐξ αὐτοῦ: from it. Latin: ex illō.
πάντες: all. Latin, omnēs.

passages.ctx: After the supper, Jesus goes out with his disciples.
passages.en: And they come to a piece of ground whose name is Gethsemane, and he says to his disciples, “Sit here until I have prayed.”

rows.note: καί, et.
ἔρχονται: they come, a vivid present. Latin: veniunt.
εἰς χωρίον: to a piece of ground, from χωρίον, a place. Latin: in praedium, an estate.
οὗ: whose, the genitive of ὅς, who. Latin uses a dative instead: cui, to which.
τὸ ὄνομα: the name, from ὄνομα. Latin: nōmen, with no article. Neither language needs a word for is.
Γεθσημανί: Gethsemane, an Aramaic name meaning oil press. Latin: Gethsemani.
καί, et.
λέγει: he says. Latin, ait.
τοῖς μαθηταῖς: to the disciples, a dative plural of μαθητής. Latin: discipulīs, also dative.
αὐτοῦ: his. Latin: suīs, his own.
καθίσατε: sit, an aorist command of καθίζω, to sit down. Latin: sedēte, from sedeō.
ὧδε: here. Latin: hīc, with a long i, unlike hic, this.
ἕως: until. Latin: dōnec.
προσεύξωμαι: I have prayed, an aorist subjunctive of προσεύχομαι, to pray. After ἕως the subjunctive looks ahead. Latin also uses a subjunctive: ōrem, from ōrō.

passages.ctx: In Gethsemane, Jesus takes three disciples aside.
passages.en: And he takes along Peter and James and John with him, and he began to be utterly dismayed and in anguish, and he says to them, “My soul is deeply grieved, all the way to death. Stay here and keep awake.”

rows.note: καί, et.
παραλαμβάνει: he takes along, from παραλαμβάνω, to take along or receive, a vivid present. Latin keeps the present: assūmit, from assūmō.
τὸν Πέτρον: Peter. Latin: Petrum, with no article.
καί, et.
Ἰάκωβον: James. Latin, Jacōbum.
καί, et.
Ἰωάννην: John. Latin, Jōannem.
μετ’ αὐτοῦ: with him. Latin: sēcum, with himself, pointing back to the subject.
καί, et.
ἤρξατο: he began, from ἄρχω. Latin: coepit.
ἐκθαμβεῖσθαι: to be utterly dismayed. Latin: pavēre, to be afraid.
καί, et.
ἀδημονεῖν: to be in anguish. Latin: taedēre, to be weary, sick at heart.
καί, et.
λέγει: he says. Latin, ait.
αὐτοῖς: to them. Latin, illīs.
περίλυπος: deeply grieved, from περί, around, and λύπη, grief. Greek puts it first. Latin: tristis, sad.
ἐστιν: is. Latin, est.
ἡ ψυχή: the soul, also life or self. Latin: anima.
μου: my. Latin, mea.
ἕως: as far as, until, with the genitive. Latin needs two words: usque ad, all the way to.
θανάτου: death, from θάνατος. Latin: mortem, from mors, accusative after ad.
μείνατε: stay, an aorist command of μένω, to remain. Latin: sustinēte, hold on, from sustineō.
ὧδε: here. Latin: hīc, with a long i.
καί, et.
γρηγορεῖτε: keep awake, from γρηγορέω, a present command. Latin: vigilāte, from vigilō, to keep watch.

passages.ctx: In Gethsemane, Jesus wakes his sleeping disciples.
passages.en: Get up, let us go. Look, the one handing me over has come near.

rows.note: ἐγείρεσθε: get up, from ἐγείρω, to raise. A plural command, passive in form: be raised. Latin: surgite, from surgō, to rise.
ἄγωμεν: let us go, from ἄγω, to lead or go. The subjunctive gives let us. Latin: eāmus, from eō, to go.
ἰδού: look. Latin: ecce.
ὁ παραδιδούς με: the one handing me over. Latin makes a clause: quī mē trādet, who will hand me over, from trādō.
ἤγγικεν: has come near, from ἐγγίζω, to draw near. A perfect: he has drawn near and is now close. Latin: prope est, is near.

nl.m: hand over, deliver; betray; hand down

passages.ctx: Jesus stands silent before Pilate.
passages.en: But Jesus no longer answered anything, so that Pilate marvelled.

rows.note: ὁ δὲ Ἰησοῦς: but Jesus. Latin: Jēsūs autem.
οὐκέτι: no longer, from οὐκ, not, and ἔτι, yet. Latin: amplius, any further.
οὐδέν: nothing, the neuter of οὐδείς, no one. Greek stacks negatives for emphasis, so English says anything. Latin: nihil, nothing.
ἀπεκρίθη: he answered, from ἀποκρίνομαι. Latin: respondit.
ὥστε: so that, introducing a result. Latin: ita ut, so that, with ita, thus.
θαυμάζειν: to marvel, from θαυμάζω. After ὥστε, Greek uses an infinitive. Latin uses a subjunctive: mīrārētur, he marvelled, from mīror.
τὸν Πιλᾶτον: Pilate, in the accusative, as the subject of an infinitive. Latin: Pīlātus, a plain nominative.

nl.m: so, thus, in this way; yes

passages.ctx: Mark explains a custom of Pilate’s at the Passover festival.
passages.en: Now at each festival he would release one prisoner to them, the one they requested.

rows.note: κατὰ δὲ ἑορτήν: now at each festival. Latin: per diem autem festum, on each feast day, with per, through, and diēs, day.
ἀπέλυεν: he would release, from ἀπολύω, an imperfect of habit. Latin: solēbat dīmittere, he used to release, from soleō and dīmittō.
αὐτοῖς: to them. Latin, illīs.
ἕνα δέσμιον: one prisoner. Latin: ūnum ex vinctīs, one of the bound.
ὃν παρῃτοῦντο: the one they requested. Latin: quemcumque petīssent, whomever they had asked for, from quīcumque, whoever, and petō, to ask.

nl.m: through, throughout; by means of; by (oaths)

passages.en: But the chief priests roused the crowd, so that he would instead release Barabbas to them.

rows.note: οἱ δὲ ἀρχιερεῖς: but the chief priests. Latin: pontificēs autem, the old Roman word for high priests.
ἀνέσεισαν: they roused, from ἀνασείω, to shake up. Latin: concitāvērunt, from concitō, to stir up.
τὸν ὄχλον: the crowd. Latin: turbam.
ἵνα: so that. Latin: ut.
μᾶλλον: instead, literally more, rather. Latin: magis, more.
τὸν Βαραββᾶν: Barabbas, in the accusative. Latin: Barabbam.
ἀπολύσῃ: he would release, a subjunctive after ἵνα. Latin: dīmitteret, also a subjunctive.
αὐτοῖς: to them. Latin, eīs.

passages.en: But Pilate kept saying to them, “What wrong, then, has he done?” Yet they shouted all the louder, “Crucify him!”

rows.note: ὁ δὲ Πιλᾶτος: but Pilate. Latin: Pīlātus vērō. vērō means in truth, here simply but.
ἔλεγεν: he kept saying, an imperfect. Latin: dīcēbat.
αὐτοῖς, illīs.
τί γάρ: what, then. Latin: quid enim.
ἐποίησεν: he did, from ποιέω, to do or make. An aorist, a single completed act. Latin: fēcit, from faciō.
κακόν: wrong, from κακός, bad or evil. Latin says what of evil, quid malī, a genitive of malus, bad.
οἱ δέ: yet they. The article alone can mean they. Latin: at illī.
περισσῶς: beyond measure, so all the louder. Latin: magis, more.
ἔκραξαν: they shouted, from κράζω, to cry out, an aorist. Latin: clāmābant, from clāmō, an imperfect: they kept shouting.
σταύρωσον: crucify, from σταυρόω. An aorist command to one person. Latin: crucifīge, from crucifīgō, to fix to a cross.
αὐτόν, eum.

passages.en: Now it was the third hour, and they crucified him.

rows.note: ἦν δέ: now it was. Latin: erat autem.
ὥρα: hour. Latin borrowed the word: hōra.
τρίτη: third, from τρίτος, feminine to agree with ὥρα. Latin: tertia, from tertius. Hours were counted from sunrise, so this is mid morning.
καί, et.
ἐσταύρωσαν: they crucified, an aorist of σταυρόω. Latin: crucifīxērunt, a perfect.
αὐτόν, eum.

passages.en: And Jesus, letting out a loud cry, breathed his last.

rows.note: ὁ δὲ Ἰησοῦς: and Jesus. Latin: Jēsūs autem.
ἀφείς: letting out, from ἀφίημι. Latin makes an ablative absolute: ēmissā vōce magnā, a loud voice sent out.
φωνήν: voice or cry, from φωνή. Latin: vōce, from vōx.
μεγάλην: great, from μέγας. Latin: magnā, from magnus.
ἐξέπνευσεν: he breathed out, from ἐκπνέω, that is, he died. Latin: expīrāvit, the root of our word expire.

passages.ctx: Three women come to the tomb of Jesus at sunrise.
passages.en: And going into the tomb, they saw a young man seated on the right, wrapped in a white robe, and they were struck with amazement.

rows.note: καί, et.
εἰσελθοῦσαι: going in, an aorist participle of εἰσέρχομαι, feminine for the women. Latin: introeuntēs, a present participle.
εἰς τὸ μνημεῖον: into the tomb, a memorial. Latin: in monumentum, from moneō, to remind.
εἶδον: they saw, the aorist of ὁράω, to see. Latin: vīdērunt, a perfect, from videō.
νεανίσκον: a young man. Latin: juvenem.
καθήμενον: seated, from κάθημαι, to sit. Latin: sedentem.
ἐν τοῖς δεξιοῖς: on the right, from δεξιός, right. Latin: in dextrīs, from dextra, right hand.
περιβεβλημένον: wrapped, a perfect participle of περιβάλλω, to throw around. Latin: coopertum, covered.
στολήν: a robe. Greek uses the accusative, Latin the ablative: stolā.
λευκήν: white. Latin: candidā, shining white.
καί, et.
ἐξεθαμβήθησαν: they were utterly amazed. Latin: obstupuērunt, they were stunned.

passages.ctx: After his resurrection, Jesus appears to the eleven disciples.
passages.en: Later, as they were reclining at table, he was revealed to the eleven, and he reproached their unbelief and hardness of heart, because they did not believe those who had seen him raised.

rows.note: ὕστερον: later. Latin: novissimē, last of all, from novus, new.
δέ: and. Latin leaves it out.
ἀνακειμένοις: reclining at table, from ἀνάκειμαι, a dative participle. Latin: recumbentibus, also dative.
αὐτοῖς, illīs.
τοῖς ἕνδεκα: the eleven, a number without endings. Latin: ūndecim.
ἐφανερώθη: he was revealed, from φανερόω, to make visible. Latin: appāruit, he appeared, from appāreō.
καί, et.
ὠνείδισεν: he reproached, from ὀνειδίζω. Latin: exprobrāvit.
τὴν ἀπιστίαν: the unbelief. Latin: incrēdulitātem.
αὐτῶν, eōrum: their.
καί, et.
σκληροκαρδίαν: hardness of heart, in one word. Latin uses two: dūritiam cordis, with cor, heart, in the genitive.
ὅτι, quia: because.
τοῖς θεασαμένοις: those who had seen, from θεάομαι. Latin uses a clause: iīs quī vīderant, from videō, to see.
αὐτὸν ἐγηγερμένον: him raised, a perfect passive participle of ἐγείρω. Latin: eum resurrēxisse, that he had risen, from resurgō.
οὐκ, nōn: not.
ἐπίστευσαν: they believed, from πιστεύω. It takes a dative, as does crēdidērunt, from crēdō.

passages.ctx: Mary answers the angel Gabriel.
passages.en: Then Mary said, “Here is the servant of the Lord. May it happen to me in keeping with your word.” And the angel went away from her.

rows.note: εἶπεν δέ: then she said. Latin: dīxit autem.
Μαριάμ: Mary, a Hebrew form without endings. Latin: Marīa.
ἰδού, ecce: here is.
ἡ δούλη: the servant, a woman slave. Latin: ancilla, handmaid. Neither language needs a verb here.
κυρίου: of the Lord. Latin: Dominī.
γένοιτο: may it happen, from γίνομαι. The optative, the mood of wishing. Latin: fīat, a subjunctive, from fīō.
μοι, mihi: to me.
κατά: according to, with the accusative. Latin: secundum, literally following, the same word as second.
τὸ ῥῆμα: the word, from ῥῆμα, a thing spoken. Latin: verbum, word.
σου: your, literally of you. Latin uses an adjective: tuum, from tuus.
καί, et.
ἀπῆλθεν: went away. Latin: discessit.
ἀπ’ αὐτῆς: from her. Latin: ab illā.
ὁ ἄγγελος: the angel, from ἄγγελος, a messenger. The double gamma is said ng. Latin borrowed it: angelus.

passages.ctx: Elizabeth greets Mary, who has come to visit her.
passages.en: And how does this happen to me, that my Lord’s mother would come to me?

rows.note: καί, et.
πόθεν: from where, here how. Latin: unde, likewise from where.
μοι, mihi: to me.
τοῦτο, hoc: this. Neither language has a verb here.
ἵνα, ut: that.
ἔλθῃ: would come, an aorist subjunctive. Latin: veniat, also subjunctive.
ἡ μήτηρ: the mother. Latin: māter. English mother shares the same root.
τοῦ κυρίου: of the Lord. Latin: Dominī.
μου: my, literally of me. Latin: meī, from meus.
πρὸς ἐμέ: to me, with the stressed form ἐμέ. Latin: ad mē.

nl.m: from where, whence; from which, hence

passages.ctx: Mary praises God in her song.
passages.en: He worked might with his arm; he scattered the arrogant in the thinking of their heart. He pulled rulers down from thrones and raised up the lowly; those who hunger he filled with good things, and those who are rich he sent off empty.

rows.note: ἐποίησεν: he worked, the aorist of ποιέω, to do or make. Latin uses the perfect: fēcit.
κράτος: might. Latin: potentiam, power.
ἐν βραχίονι: with the arm. Latin: in brachiō.
αὐτοῦ: his. suō.
διεσκόρπισεν: he scattered. dispersit.
ὑπερηφάνους: the arrogant. superbōs, the proud.
διανοίᾳ: in the thinking. mente, in mind.
καρδίας: of the heart, the genitive of καρδία, heart. Latin: cordis, from cor.
αὐτῶν: their. Latin: suī, singular, agreeing with cordis.
καθεῖλεν: he pulled down. dēposuit, he put down.
δυνάστας: rulers. potentēs, the powerful.
ἀπὸ θρόνων: from thrones, from θρόνος, throne. Latin has one seat: dē sēde.
καί, et.
ὕψωσεν: he raised up. exaltāvit.
ταπεινούς: the lowly. humilēs.
πεινῶντας: those who hunger, a present participle. Latin also: ēsurientēs.
ἐνέπλησεν: he filled. Latin: implēvit, from impleō.
ἀγαθῶν: with good things, from ἀγαθός, good. Greek uses the genitive after filling, Latin the ablative: bonīs, from bonus.
καί, et.
πλουτοῦντας: those who are rich, another participle. Latin uses an adjective: dīvitēs.
ἐξαπέστειλεν: he sent off. dīmīsit.
κενούς: empty. inānēs.

passages.ctx: Shepherds near Bethlehem on the night Jesus is born.
passages.en: And shepherds were in the same region, staying out in the fields and keeping the watches of the night over their flock.

rows.note: καί, et.
ποιμένες: shepherds, from ποιμήν. Latin: pastōrēs, from pastor.
ἦσαν, erant: they were.
ἐν τῇ χώρᾳ: in the region, from χώρα. Latin: in regiōne, from regiō.
τῇ αὐτῇ: the same, since αὐτός with the article means same. Latin: eādem, from īdem.
ἀγραυλοῦντες: staying out in the fields, from ἀγραυλέω. Latin says it differently: vigilantēs, keeping awake, from vigilō.
καί, et.
φυλάσσοντες: keeping, from φυλάσσω, to guard. Latin: custōdientēs, from custōdiō, to guard.
φυλακάς: watches, from φυλακή. Greek repeats the root: guarding guards. Latin: vigiliās.
τῆς νυκτός: of the night, from νύξ. Latin: noctis, from nox.
ἐπί: over. Latin: super.
τὴν ποίμνην: the flock, from ποίμνη. Latin: gregem, from grex.
αὐτῶν: their. Latin: suum, their own.

passages.ctx: Jesus as a boy in Nazareth.
passages.en: And the child kept growing and getting stronger, being filled with wisdom, and God’s grace was on him.

rows.note: τὸ δὲ παιδίον: and the child, from παιδίον, a little child, neuter. Latin: puer autem, from puer, boy.
ηὔξανεν: kept growing, from αὐξάνω, to grow. The imperfect, an ongoing action. Latin: crēscēbat, from crēscō.
καί, et.
ἐκραταιοῦτο: was getting stronger, from κραταιόομαι, to become strong. Latin: cōnfortābātur, he was strengthened, also an imperfect passive.
πληρούμενον: being filled, from πληρόω, to fill or fulfil. A present passive participle, neuter like the child. Latin uses an adjective: plēnus, full, masculine like puer.
σοφίᾳ: with wisdom, from σοφία, in the dative. Latin: sapientiā, from sapientia, in the ablative.
καί, et.
χάρις: grace or favor. Latin: grātia.
θεοῦ: of God, the genitive of θεός. Latin: Deī, the genitive of Deus.
ἦν: was. Latin: erat.
ἐπ’ αὐτό: on him, literally on it, since παιδίον is neuter. Latin: in illō, in him.

passages.en: And he was teaching in their synagogues, praised by everyone.

rows.note: καί, et.
αὐτός: he himself. Latin, ipse.
ἐδίδασκεν: he was teaching, an imperfect, ongoing action. Latin: docēbat.
ἐν ταῖς συναγωγαῖς: in the synagogues. Latin: in synagōgīs.
αὐτῶν: their. Latin, eōrum.
δοξαζόμενος: being praised, from δοξάζω, to glorify or praise, a present passive participle. Latin makes it a clause: et magnificābātur, and he was praised.
ὑπὸ πάντων: by all. Latin: ab omnibus.

passages.ctx: Jesus has just healed a man with leprosy.
passages.en: And he instructed him to tell no one, “Instead, go away and show yourself to the priest, and bring an offering for your cleansing just as Moses directed, as a witness to them.”

rows.note: καί, et.
αὐτός: he. Latin, ipse.
παρήγγειλεν: he instructed, from παραγγέλλω. Latin: praecēpit, from praecipiō, to command.
αὐτῷ: him, in the dative. Latin, illī.
μηδενί: to no one, a dative of μηδείς. Latin: nēminī, from nēmō, no one.
εἰπεῖν: to tell, an aorist infinitive of λέγω. Latin uses a clause: ut dīceret, that he should tell.
ἀλλά: but, here instead. The report turns into direct speech. Latin: sed.
ἀπελθών: going away, an aorist participle of ἀπέρχομαι. Latin uses a command: vāde, go, from vādō.
δεῖξον: show, an aorist command, from δείκνυμι. Latin: ostende, from ostendō, to show.
σεαυτόν: yourself, from σεαυτοῦ, the reflexive pronoun. Latin simply says tē, you.
τῷ ἱερεῖ: to the priest, a dative, from ἱερεύς. Latin: sacerdōtī, from sacerdōs.
καί, et.
προσένεγκε: offer, an aorist command from προσφέρω, to bring, to offer. Latin: offer, from offerō.
περί: about, concerning; here, for. Latin: prō, for, on behalf of.
τοῦ καθαρισμοῦ: the cleansing, from καθαρισμός. Latin: ēmundātiōne, from ēmundātiō.
σου: your, literally of you. Latin uses an adjective, tuā, agreeing with cleansing.
καθώς: just as. Latin: sīcut.
προσέταξεν: he directed, from προστάσσω, to command. Latin repeats praecēpit.
Μωϋσῆς: Moses. Latin: Mōysēs.
εἰς μαρτύριον: as a witness, literally into a witness. Latin keeps the idiom: in testimōnium.
αὐτοῖς: to them. Latin: illīs.

nl.m: for, on behalf of; in place of; before

passages.ctx: Jesus, shortly before he chooses the twelve apostles.
passages.en: Now during these days it happened that he went out to the mountain to pray, and he was spending the whole night in prayer to God.

rows.note: ἐγένετο: it happened. Latin: factum est.
δέ, autem: now.
ἐν ταῖς ἡμέραις: in the days, from ἡμέρα, day. Latin: in diēbus, from diēs.
ταύταις: these. Latin says those: illīs.
ἐξελθεῖν: to go out, an infinitive: it happened for him to go out. Latin uses a plain verb, exiit, he went out.
αὐτόν: him, the accusative subject of the infinitive. Latin leaves it out.
εἰς τὸ ὄρος: to the mountain, from ὄρος. Latin: in montem, from mōns.
προσεύξασθαι: to pray, from προσεύχομαι, an infinitive of purpose. Latin: ōrāre, from ōrō.
καί, et.
ἦν, erat: he was.
διανυκτερεύων: spending the whole night, a participle built on νύξ, night. Latin builds the same way: pernoctāns, on nox.
ἐν τῇ προσευχῇ: in prayer, from προσευχή, kin to the verb. Latin: in ōrātiōne, from ōrātiō, kin to ōrō.
τοῦ θεοῦ: of God, meaning prayer to God. Latin: Deī.

passages.en: For each tree is recognized by its own fruit. For people do not collect figs from thorn plants, nor do they harvest grapes from a bramble.

rows.note: ἕκαστον: each, from ἕκαστος, neuter to match tree. Latin: ūnaquaeque, from ūnusquisque, feminine like arbor.
γάρ: for. Latin: enim. Both stand second in the clause.
δένδρον: tree. Latin: arbor.
ἐκ τοῦ ἰδίου: by its own, from ἴδιος, one’s own. Latin: dē and suō.
καρποῦ: fruit, from καρπός. Latin: frūctū, from frūctus.
γινώσκεται: is recognized, literally is known, a present passive. Latin: cognōscitur.
οὐ γάρ: for not. Latin: neque enim. neque means nor.
ἐξ ἀκανθῶν: from thorn plants. ἐκ becomes ἐξ before a vowel. Latin: dē spīnīs.
συλλέγουσιν: they collect, from συλλέγω. Latin: colligunt, from colligō.
σῦκα: figs, plural of σῦκον. Latin: fīcūs.
οὐδέ: nor. Latin, neque again.
ἐκ βάτου: from a bramble, from βάτος. Latin: dē rubō.
σταφυλήν: a bunch of grapes, from σταφυλή. Latin: ūvam, from ūva.
τρυγῶσιν: they harvest, from τρυγάω. Latin: vindēmiant, they gather grapes.

nl.m: and not, nor; neque … neque neither … nor

passages.ctx: A Roman centurion’s valued slave is sick and close to death.
passages.en: Hearing about Jesus, he sent elders of the Jews to him, asking him to come and rescue his slave.

rows.note: ἀκούσας: hearing, an aorist participle. Latin uses a clause: cum audīsset, when he had heard.
δέ: and, or now. Latin: et.
περὶ τοῦ Ἰησοῦ: about Jesus. Latin: dē Jēsū.
ἀπέστειλεν: he sent, from ἀποστέλλω, to send out, the source of apostle. Latin: mīsit, from mittō.
πρὸς αὐτόν: to him. Latin: ad eum.
πρεσβυτέρους: elders, from πρεσβύτερος, older. Latin: seniōrēs, older men, from senex, old.
τῶν Ἰουδαίων: of the Jews, a genitive, from Ἰουδαῖος. Latin: Jūdaeōrum, from Jūdaeus.
ἐρωτῶν: asking, a present participle of ἐρωτάω. Latin: rogāns.
αὐτόν, eum.
ὅπως: that, introducing the request. Latin: ut.
ἐλθών: coming, a participle of ἔρχομαι. Latin makes it a verb: venīret et, that he come and.
διασώσῃ: he might rescue, from διασῴζω, to bring safely through. Latin: salvāret, from salvō.
τὸν δοῦλον: the slave, from δοῦλος, slave or servant. Latin: servum, from servus.
αὐτοῦ: his. Latin, ejus.

passages.ctx: At Nain, Jesus meets the funeral of a widow’s only son.
passages.en: And approaching, he touched the bier; the men carrying it came to a stop, and he said, “Young man, I tell you, get up!”

rows.note: καί, et.
προσελθών: approaching, from προσέρχομαι, to come to. Latin makes it a verb, accessit, from accēdō, to approach.
ἥψατο: he touched, from ἅπτω. Latin: tetigit, from tangō.
τῆς σοροῦ: the bier, a genitive after touch. Latin: loculum.
οἱ δέ: and those. Latin: hī autem.
βαστάζοντες: carrying, from βαστάζω. Latin: quī portābant, who carried.
ἔστησαν: they came to a stop, from ἵστημι, to stand. Latin: stetērunt, from stō.
καί, et.
εἶπεν: he said. Latin: ait.
Νεανίσκε: young man, a vocative. Latin: adolēscēns.
σοί: to you, placed first for emphasis. Latin: tibi.
λέγω: I tell. Latin: dīcō.
ἐγέρθητι: get up, an aorist passive command of ἐγείρω. Latin: surge.

passages.ctx: From the parable of the sower.
passages.en: And another fell in the midst of the thorns, and the thorns, growing up with it, choked it.

rows.note: καί, et.
ἕτερον: another, neuter, from ἕτερος, other. Latin: aliud, the neuter of alius, other.
ἔπεσεν: it fell, the aorist of πίπτω, to fall. Latin: cecidit, from cadō, to fall.
ἐν μέσῳ: in the midst of, from μέσος, middle. Latin uses one word: inter, among.
τῶν ἀκανθῶν: of the thorns. Latin: spīnās, an accusative after inter.
καί, et.
συμφυεῖσαι: growing up together, from συμφύομαι, feminine to match the thorns. Latin: simul exortae, springing up together, from exorior.
αἱ ἄκανθαι: the thorns, now the subject. Latin: spīnae.
ἀπέπνιξαν: they choked, from ἀποπνίγω. Latin: suffōcāvērunt, from suffōcō.
αὐτό: it, neuter. Latin: illud.

nl.m: other, another; aliī … aliī some … others

passages.ctx: Jesus explains the parable of the sower.
passages.en: Now no one, having lit a lamp, covers it with a jar or puts it under a bed, but he puts it on a lampstand, so that those coming in may see the light.

rows.note: οὐδείς: no one. Latin: nēmō.
δέ, autem.
λύχνον: a lamp. Latin: lucernam.
ἅψας: having lit. An aorist participle of ἅπτω. Latin uses a present participle: accendēns, lighting.
καλύπτει αὐτόν: covers it. αὐτόν is masculine, like λύχνος. Latin: operit eam, feminine, like lucerna.
σκεύει: with a vessel, a jar. A dative of means. Latin uses the ablative: vāse.
ἤ: or. Latin: aut.
ὑποκάτω κλίνης: under a bed. ὑποκάτω takes the genitive. Latin: subtus lectum.
τίθησιν: he puts, from τίθημι, to put or place. Latin: pōnit, from pōnō.
ἀλλά: but. Latin: sed.
ἐπὶ λυχνίας: on a lampstand, with the genitive. Latin: suprā candēlābrum, using suprā, above or on top of.
τίθησιν again: he puts. pōnit.
ἵνα: so that. Latin: ut.
οἱ εἰσπορευόμενοι: those coming in. A participle with the article. Latin needs no article: intrantēs.
βλέπωσιν: they may see, from βλέπω, to see. A subjunctive after ἵνα. Latin: videant, also subjunctive.
τὸ φῶς: the light, from φῶς. Latin: lūmen.

passages.ctx: Jesus has said that the daughter of Jairus is not dead but asleep.
passages.en: And they were laughing at him, knowing that she had died.

rows.note: καί, et.
κατεγέλων: they were laughing at, from καταγελάω. Latin: dērīdēbant, they mocked.
αὐτοῦ: him, a genitive. Latin: eum.
εἰδότες: knowing, from οἶδα. Latin: scientēs, from sciō, to know.
ὅτι: that. Latin: quod.
ἀπέθανεν: she died, from ἀποθνῄσκω, to die. Latin: mortua esset, from morior. mortua is feminine.

passages.ctx: Jesus has sent out the twelve.
passages.en: And setting out, they went from village to village, announcing the good news and healing everywhere.

rows.note: ἐξερχόμενοι: going out, a present participle. Latin: ēgressī, having gone out, a perfect participle.
δέ, autem.
διήρχοντο: they went about, the imperfect of διέρχομαι, to pass through. Latin: circuībant, they went around.
κατὰ τὰς κώμας: from village to village, from κώμη. Latin: per castella, through the villages.
εὐαγγελιζόμενοι: announcing the good news, from εὐαγγελίζω. Latin simply borrows the word: ēvangelīzantēs.
καί, et.
θεραπεύοντες: healing, from θεραπεύω, to heal. Latin: cūrantēs, from cūrō, to care for.
πανταχοῦ: everywhere. Latin: ubīque.

passages.en: For just as Jonah became a sign for the Ninevites, so also will the Son of Man be for this generation.

rows.note: καθώς: just as. Latin: sīcut.
γάρ: for. Latin: nam, for, which comes first in its clause, unlike enim.
ἐγένετο: became, from γίνομαι. Latin: fuit, was.
Ἰωνᾶς: Jonah. Latin: Jōnās.
τοῖς Νινευίταις: for the Ninevites, a dative. Latin: Nīnivītīs, also a dative.
σημεῖον: a sign. Latin: signum, a sign, placed before the Ninevites.
οὕτως: so, in this way. It answers καθώς: just as, so. Latin: ita.
ἔσται: will be, the future of εἰμί. Latin: erit.
καί here means also. Latin: et, also.
ὁ υἱός: the son, from υἱός. Latin: fīlius, son.
τοῦ ἀνθρώπου: of man, the genitive of ἄνθρωπος, human being. Latin: hominis, from homō.
τῇ γενεᾷ: for the generation, the dative of γενεά. Latin: generātiōnī, from generātiō.
ταύτῃ: this. Latin: istī.

passages.ctx: Jesus speaks to the experts in the law.
passages.en: Woe to you, because you build the tombs of the prophets, but your fathers killed them.

rows.note: οὐαί: woe. Latin: vae.
ὑμῖν: to you, plural. Latin: vōbīs.
ὅτι: because. Latin says quī instead, you who.
οἰκοδομεῖτε: you build, from οἰκοδομέω. Latin: aedificātis.
τὰ μνημεῖα: the tombs, from μνημεῖον, a memorial or tomb. Latin: monumenta, from monumentum.
τῶν προφητῶν: of the prophets, from προφήτης, a masculine noun that follows the feminine pattern. Latin: prophētārum, from prophēta, likewise.
οἱ δὲ πατέρες: but the fathers, plural of πατήρ, father. Latin: patrēs autem, from pater, with no word for the.
ὑμῶν: your, literally of you. Latin uses an adjective: vestrī, from vester, your, said to many.
ἀπέκτειναν: they killed, from ἀποκτείνω, to kill. Latin: occīdērunt, from occīdō, to kill.
αὐτούς: them. Latin: illōs.

passages.ctx: Jesus speaks of a debtor taken before a judge.
passages.en: I tell you, you will never get out of there until you have paid even the last small coin.

rows.note: λέγω, dīcō.
σοι, tibi: to you.
οὐ μή: a double negative, never. Latin: nōn.
ἐξέλθῃς: you get out, an aorist subjunctive. Latin uses the future: exiēs, a later form of exībis.
ἐκεῖθεν: from there. Latin: inde.
ἕως: until. Latin: dōnec.
καί: here, even. Latin: etiam, also or even.
τὸ ἔσχατον: the last, from ἔσχατος. Latin: novissimum, the newest, from novus, here meaning last.
λεπτόν: a tiny copper coin, literally thin. Latin: minūtum, a small coin.
ἀποδῷς: you pay back, an aorist subjunctive of ἀποδίδωμι, to give back. Latin: reddās, from reddō.

passages.en: Now some were present at that very time, reporting to him about the Galileans whose blood Pilate had mixed with their sacrifices.

rows.note: παρῆσαν: they were present, an imperfect of πάρειμι. Latin: aderant, from adsum.
δέ, autem.
τινες: some, from τις, a certain one. Latin: quīdam.
ἐν αὐτῷ τῷ καιρῷ: at that very time. αὐτῷ here means very. καιρός: time, season. Latin: ipsō in tempore, from tempus.
ἀπαγγέλλοντες: reporting, a present participle of ἀπαγγέλλω, to report, to announce. Latin: nūntiantēs, from nūntiō.
αὐτῷ: to him. Latin: illī.
περί: about. Latin: dē.
τῶν Γαλιλαίων: the Galileans, genitive after περί. Latin puts them in the ablative after dē: Galilaeīs.
ὧν: whose, the genitive plural of ὅς. Latin: quōrum.
τὸ αἷμα: the blood. Latin: sanguinem, from sanguis, blood.
Πιλᾶτος, Pīlātus.
ἔμιξεν: he mixed, from μίγνυμι. Latin: miscuit, from misceō, a cousin of our word mix.
μετά: with. Latin: cum.
τῶν θυσιῶν: the sacrifices, from θυσία. Latin: sacrificiīs, ablative after cum, from sacrificium.
αὐτῶν: their. Latin: eōrum.

passages.en: No, I tell you. But unless you repent, you will all perish in the same way.

rows.note: οὐχί: no, a strong οὐ. Latin: nōn.
λέγω, dīcō.
ὑμῖν, vōbīs: to you.
ἀλλά: but. Latin: sed.
ἐὰν μή: if not, unless. ἐάν takes the subjunctive. Latin: sī, if, then nōn.
μετανοῆτε: you repent, from μετανοέω. Latin uses a phrase: poenitentiam ēgeritis, you will have done penance, from poenitentia, repentance.
πάντες, omnēs: all.
ὡσαύτως: likewise, in the same way. Latin: similiter, similarly.
ἀπολεῖσθε: you will perish, a future middle of ἀπόλλυμι, to destroy. In the middle it means to perish. Latin: perībitis, from pereō.

passages.ctx: Jesus tells what the kingdom of God is like.
passages.en: It is like yeast, which a woman took and hid in three measures of flour until the whole was leavened.

rows.note: ὁμοία: like, from ὅμοιος. It takes the dative. Latin: simile, from similis.
ἐστίν, est: it is.
ζύμῃ: yeast, dative. Latin: fermentō.
ἥν: which, feminine like yeast. Latin quod is neuter like fermentum.
λαβοῦσα: having taken, from λαμβάνω. Latin turns it around: acceptum, having been taken, a passive participle.
γυνή: woman. Compare gynecology. Latin: mulier.
ἔκρυψεν: she hid, from κρύπτω. Compare cryptic. Latin: abscondit.
εἰς: into. Latin: in.
ἀλεύρου: of flour. Latin: farīnae.
σάτα: measures, a Hebrew measure. Latin borrows it: sata.
τρία: three, from τρεῖς. Latin: tria, from trēs.
ἕως οὗ: until. Latin: dōnec.
ἐζυμώθη: it was leavened, an aorist passive of ζυμόω. Latin: fermentārētur, a subjunctive after dōnec.
ὅλον: the whole, from ὅλος. Compare holistic. Latin: tōtum, from tōtus. Compare total.

passages.ctx: Jesus is on his long journey.
passages.en: And he was traveling through cities and villages, teaching and making his way to Jerusalem.

rows.note: καί, et.
διεπορεύετο: he was traveling through, an imperfect of διαπορεύομαι. Latin: ībat, he was going, from eō.
κατά: throughout. Latin: per.
πόλεις: cities, from πόλις. Compare metropolis. Latin: cīvitātēs, from cīvitās.
καί, et.
κώμας: villages. Latin: castella, little forts.
διδάσκων, docēns: teaching.
καί, et.
πορείαν ποιούμενος: making a journey, with a middle participle of ποιέω. Latin: iter faciēns, word for word.
εἰς Ἱεροσόλυμα: to Jerusalem, here a neuter plural form. Latin: in Jerusalem, which does not decline.

passages.ctx: In the parable, invited guests make excuses for missing a great dinner.
passages.en: And another said, ‘I married a wife, and for this reason I am not able to come.’

rows.note: καί, et.
ἕτερος: another. Latin: alius.
εἶπεν, dīxit: he said.
γυναῖκα: wife, the accusative of γυνή. Latin uses a separate word: uxōrem, from uxor, wife.
ἔγημα: I married, an aorist of γαμέω. Compare monogamy. Latin says uxōrem dūxī, I led a wife, from dūcō, to lead, the usual idiom.
καί, et.
διὰ τοῦτο: for this reason. διά, through, with the accusative means because of. Latin: ideō, therefore.
οὐ, nōn.
δύναμαι: I am able. Compare dynamic. It is middle in form, active in meaning. Latin: possum, I can.
ἐλθεῖν: to come, from ἔρχομαι. Latin: venīre.

passages.ctx: Jesus ends the parable of the lost sheep.
passages.en: I tell you that in the same way there will be joy in heaven over one sinner who repents, more than over ninety-nine righteous people who have no need of repentance.

rows.note: λέγω, dīcō.
ὑμῖν, vōbīs: to you.
ὅτι: that. Latin: quod.
οὕτως: so, in this way. Latin: ita.
χαρά: joy. Latin: gaudium, joy.
ἐν τῷ οὐρανῷ: in heaven. Latin: in caelō.
ἔσται: there will be, the future of εἰμί. Latin: erit, placed before the words in heaven.
ἐπί: over. Latin: super.
ἑνί: one, the dative of εἷς. Latin: ūnō.
ἁμαρτωλῷ: sinner, from ἁμαρτωλός, sinful, a sinner. Latin: peccātōre, from peccātor.
μετανοοῦντι: repenting, a participle of μετανοέω. Latin again uses a phrase: poenitentiam agente, doing penance.
ἤ: or, and after a comparison, than. Latin: quam, than.
ἐπί, super.
ἐνενήκοντα ἐννέα: ninety-nine. ἐννέα is nine. Latin: nōnāgintā novem.
δικαίοις: righteous people, from δίκαιος, just, righteous. Latin: jūstīs, from jūstus.
οἵτινες: who, from ὅστις, whoever. It often means people of the sort who. Latin: quī.
οὐ, nōn.
χρείαν ἔχουσιν: they have need, from χρεία, need. Latin uses one verb: indigent, they need, from indigeō.
μετανοίας: of repentance, the genitive of μετάνοια. Latin: poenitentiā, in the ablative, which indigeō often takes.

passages.ctx: Jesus has just taught about serving God or money.
passages.en: Now the Pharisees, being fond of money, were listening to all these things, and they were sneering at him.

rows.note: ἤκουον: they were listening, an imperfect. Latin: audiēbant.
δέ, autem.
ταῦτα, haec: these things.
πάντα, omnia: all.
οἱ Φαρισαῖοι, Pharisaeī.
φιλάργυροι: money-loving, literally silver-loving. Latin: avārī, greedy.
ὑπάρχοντες: being, from ὑπάρχω, to be, to exist. Latin makes a clause: quī erant, who were.
καί, et.
ἐξεμυκτήριζον: they were sneering, literally turning up the nose. Latin: dērīdēbant, they were laughing at.
αὐτόν: him. Latin: illum.

passages.en: And the apostles said to the Lord, ‘Grant us more faith.’

rows.note: καί, et.
εἶπαν: they said. Latin: dīxērunt.
οἱ ἀπόστολοι: the apostles, from ἀπόστολος, one who is sent out. Latin borrows the word: apostolī, from apostolus.
τῷ κυρίῳ: to the Lord, in the dative. Latin: Dominō.
πρόσθες: add, an aorist imperative of προστίθημι, to add. Latin: adaugē, increase, from adaugeō.
ἡμῖν: to us. Latin: nōbīs, from nōs, we.
πίστιν: faith, from πίστις, faith, trust. Latin: fidem, from fidēs. Compare fidelity.

passages.en: And a certain ruler questioned him, saying, ‘Good teacher, by doing what will I inherit eternal life?’

rows.note: καί, et.
ἐπηρώτησεν: he questioned, an aorist of ἐπερωτάω, to ask. Latin: interrogāvit, from interrogō.
τις: a certain. Latin: quīdam.
αὐτόν: him. Latin: eum.
ἄρχων: a ruler, from ἄρχω, to rule. Latin: princeps, a leading man. Compare prince.
λέγων, dīcēns: saying.
διδάσκαλε: teacher, the vocative of διδάσκαλος, for direct address. Latin: magister, unchanged in the vocative.
ἀγαθέ: good, also vocative. Latin: bone, from bonus.
τί: what. Latin: quid.
ποιήσας: having done, an aorist participle of ποιέω. Latin has no active past participle, so it uses the present: faciēns, doing.
ζωήν: life, from ζωή. Compare zoology. Latin: vītam, from vīta.
αἰώνιον: eternal, from αἰώνιος, with one ending for masculine and feminine. Latin: aeternam, from aeternus.
κληρονομήσω: I will inherit, from κληρονομέω. Latin: possidēbō, I will possess, from possideō.

passages.ctx: A blind man by the road near Jericho hears that Jesus is passing.
passages.en: And he shouted, saying, “Jesus, Son of David, have mercy on me!”

rows.note: καί, et.
ἐβόησεν: he shouted, from βοάω. Latin: clāmāvit.
λέγων, dīcēns.
Ἰησοῦ, Jēsū: Jesus, the vocative.
υἱέ, fīlī: son, also vocative.
Δαυίδ, Dāvīd: of David. The name never changes.
ἐλέησον: have mercy, an aorist command. Latin: miserēre, from misereor.
με: me. Latin uses the genitive, meī.

passages.ctx: Jesus has told Zacchaeus to come down from the tree.
passages.en: And hurrying, he came down and welcomed him with joy.

rows.note: καί, et.
σπεύσας: hurrying, from σπεύδω, to hurry. An aorist participle. Latin: festīnāns, from festīnō.
κατέβη: he came down, from καταβαίνω, to go down. Latin: dēscendit, from dēscendō.
καί, et.
ὑπεδέξατο: he welcomed, from ὑποδέχομαι, to receive as a guest. Latin: excēpit, from excipiō.
αὐτόν: him. Latin: illum.
χαίρων: rejoicing, from χαίρω, to rejoice, a present participle. Latin: gaudēns, from gaudeō.

passages.ctx: Jesus speaks at the house of Zacchaeus.
passages.en: And Jesus said to him, “Today salvation has come about for this house, because he too is a son of Abraham. For the Son of Man came to search for and save what has been lost.”

rows.note: εἶπεν δέ: and he said. Latin: ait, with no word for and.
πρὸς αὐτόν: to him. Latin: ad eum.
ὁ Ἰησοῦς, Jēsūs.
ὅτι here just opens the quotation. Latin keeps it as quia.
σήμερον: today. It never changes form. Latin: hodiē.
σωτηρία: salvation, a feminine noun from the root of to save. Latin: salūs, safety, salvation.
τῷ οἴκῳ τούτῳ: for this house. οἶκος means house, here in the dative. Latin: domuī huic.
ἐγένετο: has come about, literally came to be. Latin: facta est.
καθότι: because, inasmuch as. Latin: eō quod, for the reason that.
καί: here too, also. Latin: et.
αὐτός: he himself. Latin: ipse.
υἱὸς Ἀβραάμ: a son of Abraham. Latin: fīlius Abrahae, giving the name a genitive ending.
ἐστιν: is. Latin uses the subjunctive, sit.
ἦλθεν: came. Latin: vēnit, the perfect, with a long e.
γάρ: for. Latin: enim.
ὁ υἱός, Fīlius.
τοῦ ἀνθρώπου: of man, the genitive. Latin: hominis.
ζητῆσαι: to search for, from ζητέω, to seek. An aorist infinitive. Latin: quaerere, from quaerō.
καί, et.
σῶσαι: to save, from σῴζω. Latin needs two words: salvum facere, to make safe, from salvus.
τὸ ἀπολωλός: what has been lost, a perfect participle: lost and still lost. Latin uses a clause, quod perierat, what had perished.

passages.ctx: In the parable, the servants report to their master.
passages.en: And the second one came, saying, “Your mina, master, has produced five minas.”

rows.note: καί, et.
ἦλθεν: came. Latin: vēnit.
ὁ δεύτερος: the second. Latin: alter, the other, or the second of two.
λέγων, dīcēns.
ἡ μνᾶ: the mina, a sum of money, about a hundred drachmas. Latin borrows the word: mna.
σου: your. Latin: tua.
κύριε: master, the vocative. Latin puts it first: Domine.
ἐποίησεν: made, here produced. Latin: fēcit.
πέντε: five, which never changes. Latin: quīnque.
μνᾶς: minas, accusative plural. Latin: mnās.

passages.ctx: In the parable, the owner sends a third servant.
passages.en: And he went on to send a third; but this one too they wounded and threw out.

rows.note: καί, et.
προσέθετο: he added, so he went on. Latin: addidit, from addō.
τρίτον: a third, or a third time. Latin: tertium.
πέμψαι: to send, an aorist infinitive of πέμπω. Latin: mittere.
οἱ δέ: but they. Latin: quī, who.
καί: also. Latin: et.
τοῦτον: this one. Latin: illum.
τραυματίσαντες: having wounded, from τραυματίζω. Latin: vulnerantēs.
ἐξέβαλον: they threw out. Latin: ējēcērunt, from ējiciō, to cast out.

nl.m: throw out, cast out, drive out

passages.en: And going out, he went, according to his custom, to the Mount of Olives; and the disciples also followed him.

rows.note: καί, et.
ἐξελθών: going out, an aorist participle. Latin: ēgressus, having gone out.
ἐπορεύθη: he went, from πορεύομαι, to go. Passive in form, active in meaning. Latin: ībat, he was going.
κατὰ τὸ ἔθος: according to custom; ἔθος is a habit. Latin: secundum cōnsuētūdinem.
εἰς τὸ ὄρος: to the mountain. Latin: in monte, from mōns, an ablative: on the mount, not to it.
τῶν Ἐλαιῶν: of the olives, from ἐλαία. Latin: olīvārum, from olīva.
ἠκολούθησαν: they followed, from ἀκολουθέω. Latin: secūtī sunt, from sequor, again passive in form, active in meaning.
δέ, autem.
αὐτῷ: him, in the dative, which this verb takes. Latin uses the accusative, illum.
καί: also. Latin: et.
οἱ μαθηταί: the disciples. Latin: discipulī.

passages.ctx: The council has just heard Jesus speak.
passages.en: But they said, “What further need of testimony do we have? For we ourselves heard it from his mouth.”

rows.note: οἱ δέ: but they. Latin: at illī.
εἶπαν: they said. Latin: dīxērunt.
τί: what. Latin: quid.
ἔτι: still, further, an adverb. Latin: adhūc, still, as yet.
ἔχομεν: we have. Latin has dēsīderāmus, we desire, from dēsīderō.
μαρτυρίας: of testimony, from μαρτυρία. Latin: testimōnium, the object.
χρείαν: need. Latin drops it, since dēsīderāmus already carries the sense.
αὐτοί: we ourselves. Latin: ipsī.
γάρ, enim.
ἠκούσαμεν: we heard. Latin: audīvimus.
ἀπὸ τοῦ στόματος: from the mouth. στόμα, mouth, is a neuter noun. Latin: dē ōre, from ōs, mouth, with a long o.
αὐτοῦ: his. Latin: ejus.

passages.ctx: One of the criminals crucified with Jesus rebukes the other.
passages.en: And we, for our part, are here justly, for we are getting back things worthy of what we did; but this man did nothing wrong.

rows.note: καί, et.
ἡμεῖς, nōs: we.
μέν: for our part, looking ahead to a matching δέ. Latin: quidem, indeed.
δικαίως, jūstē: justly, both adverbs.
ἄξια: worthy things, from ἄξιος. Latin: digna, from dignus.
γάρ, nam: for.
ὧν ἐπράξαμεν: of what we did, from πράσσω, to do. Latin has one word, factīs, deeds, an ablative with digna.
ἀπολαμβάνομεν: we are getting back, from ἀπολαμβάνω. Latin: recipimus, from recipiō.
οὗτος, hic: this man.
δέ, vērō: but.
οὐδέν, nihil: nothing.
ἄτοπον: wrong, literally out of place. Latin: malī, of evil, after nihil.
ἔπραξεν: did. Latin: gessit, from gerō.

nl.m: indeed, certainly; nē … quidem not even

passages.ctx: The risen Jesus suddenly stands among his disciples.
passages.en: But startled and becoming terrified, they thought they were seeing a spirit.

rows.note: πτοηθέντες: startled, an aorist passive participle of πτοέομαι. Latin: conturbātī, thrown into confusion.
δέ, vērō: but.
καί, et.
ἔμφοβοι γενόμενοι: becoming terrified, literally in fear. Latin has one word, conterritī.
ἐδόκουν: they thought, from δοκέω, to think or to seem. An imperfect. Latin: existimābant.
πνεῦμα: a spirit, a neuter noun, also breath or wind. Latin: spīritum, from spīritus.
θεωρεῖν: to be seeing, from θεωρέω, to look at. Latin: vidēre, with sē, themselves, as its subject.

passages.ctx: John speaks of the Word.
passages.en: This one was in the beginning with God.

rows.note: οὗτος: this one. Latin has the neuter, hoc, because verbum, the Word, is neuter in Latin.
ἦν, erat.
ἐν ἀρχῇ: in the beginning, from ἀρχή, beginning or rule. Latin: in prīncipiō.
πρός: here with, or facing. Latin: apud, beside, in the presence of.
τὸν θεόν: God. Latin: Deum.

nl.m: at, near, with, among; at the houseof

passages.ctx: The Gospel writer speaks of John the Baptist.
passages.en: That man was not the light, but came so that he might testify about the light.

rows.note: οὐκ: not. Latin: nōn.
ἦν, erat.
ἐκεῖνος: that man, pointing farther off than οὗτος. Latin: ille.
τὸ φῶς: the light, from φῶς, a neuter noun. Latin: lūx.
ἀλλά: but, shortened before a vowel. Latin: sed.
ἵνα: so that. Latin: ut. English adds came.
μαρτυρήσῃ: he might testify, from μαρτυρέω, an aorist subjunctive after ἵνα. Latin uses two words, testimōnium perhibēret, he might bear witness, from perhibeō.
περί: about. Latin: dē.
τοῦ φωτός: the light, genitive after περί. Latin varies the word: lūmine, from lūmen.

passages.en: There was the true light, which illumines every human being coming into the world.

rows.note: ἦν: was. Latin: erat.
τὸ φῶς: the light. Latin: lūx.
τὸ ἀληθινόν: the true. Greek repeats the article: the light, the true one. Latin: vēra, from vērus, true.
ὅ: which. Latin quae is feminine, like lūx.
φωτίζει: illumines, gives light to, from φωτίζω. Latin: illūminat, from illūminō.
πάντα: every. Latin: omnem.
ἄνθρωπον: human being. Latin: hominem.
ἐρχόμενον: coming. Latin: venientem.
εἰς: into. Latin: in, with the accusative.
τὸν κόσμον: the world, from κόσμος. Latin adds a word: hunc mundum, this world, from mundus.

passages.ctx: John the Baptist answers those sent to question him.
passages.en: He declared, “I am a voice of someone shouting in the desert: ‘Straighten the way of the Lord,’ just as Isaiah the prophet said.”

rows.note: ἔφη: he declared, from φημί, to say, to declare. Latin: ait.
ἐγώ, ego: I. Neither language needs a word for am.
φωνή: a voice. Latin: vōx.
βοῶντος: of someone shouting, a participle in the genitive. Latin: clāmantis, the same.
ἐν τῇ ἐρήμῳ: in the desert. ἔρημος means deserted; with the feminine article, the desert. Latin: in dēsertō, an abandoned place, from dēserō, to abandon.
εὐθύνατε: straighten, from εὐθύνω, an aorist command, plural. Latin: dīrigite, from dīrigō.
τὴν ὁδόν: the way, from ὁδός, feminine despite its ending. Latin: viam, from via.
κυρίου: of the Lord. Latin: Dominī.
καθώς: just as. Latin: sīcut.
εἶπεν: said. Latin: dīxit.
Ἠσαΐας: Isaiah. Latin: Isaīās.
ὁ προφήτης: the prophet. Latin borrows the Greek word: prophēta.

passages.ctx: Jesus has just met Simon Peter.
passages.en: On the next day he wanted to go out into Galilee, and he finds Philip, and Jesus says to him, “Follow me.”

rows.note: τῇ ἐπαύριον: on the next day. The feminine article implies the word day. Latin: in crastinum, for the morrow.
ἠθέλησεν: he wanted, from θέλω, to want or wish. Latin: voluit, the perfect of volō, to want.
ἐξελθεῖν: to go out, an aorist infinitive of ἐξέρχομαι. Latin: exīre.
εἰς τὴν Γαλιλαίαν: into Galilee. Latin: in Galīlaeam, with no article.
καί, et.
εὑρίσκει: he finds, from εὑρίσκω, to find. A vivid present. Latin: invenit, from inveniō.
Φίλιππον: Philip. Philippum.
καί, et.
λέγει: says. Latin, dīcit.
αὐτῷ: to him. Latin, eī.
ὁ Ἰησοῦς: Jesus. Latin, Jēsūs, without the article.
ἀκολούθει μοι: follow me. ἀκολουθέω takes the dative, μοι. Latin: sequere mē, from sequor, with the accusative.

passages.ctx: At a wedding in Cana, the wine has run out.
passages.en: Jesus says to them, “Fill the jars with water.” And they filled them right up to the top.

rows.note: λέγει, dīcit.
αὐτοῖς, eīs.
ὁ Ἰησοῦς, Jēsūs.
γεμίσατε: fill, a plural command, from γεμίζω. Latin: implēte, from impleō.
τὰς ὑδρίας: the water jars, from ὑδρία. Latin borrows the word: hydriās.
ὕδατος: with water, from ὕδωρ, water. Greek verbs of filling take the genitive. Latin uses the ablative: aquā, from aqua.
καί, et.
ἐγέμισαν: they filled. Latin, the perfect: implēvērunt.
αὐτάς: them, the jars. eās.
ἕως: right up to. Latin uses two words, usque ad.
ἄνω: above. Latin: summum, the top, from summus.

passages.ctx: In the temple, the Jews ask Jesus for a sign.
passages.en: Jesus answered and said to them, “Tear down this temple, and in three days I will raise it.”

rows.note: ἀπεκρίθη: he answered, from ἀποκρίνομαι. Latin: respondit.
Ἰησοῦς, Jēsūs.
καί, et.
εἶπεν: said. dīxit.
αὐτοῖς, eīs.
λύσατε: tear down, from λύω, to loose or undo. An aorist imperative, plural. Latin: solvite, from solvō, to loosen.
τὸν ναόν: the temple, from ναός, the sanctuary itself. Latin: templum, with no article.
τοῦτον: this, masculine like ναός. Latin: hoc, neuter, to match templum.
καί, et.
ἐν τρισίν: in three, the dative of τρεῖς. Latin: in tribus.
ἡμέραις: days, from ἡμέρα, day. A dative of time. Latin: diēbus, ablative, from diēs.
ἐγερῶ: I will raise, the future of ἐγείρω. Latin: excitābō, from excitō, to rouse.
αὐτόν: it, masculine for the temple. Latin: illud, neuter.

passages.ctx: Jesus is leaving Judea for Galilee.
passages.en: Now it was necessary for him to pass through Samaria.

rows.note: ἔδει: it was necessary, from δεῖ. Latin: oportēbat.
δέ, autem.
αὐτόν: him, with the infinitive. eum.
διέρχεσθαι: to pass through. Latin: trānsīre, from trānseō, to go across.
διὰ τῆς Σαμαρείας: through Samaria, with the genitive. Latin: per Samarīam.

nl.m: go across, pass over; pass by; pass away

passages.ctx: Jesus speaks with a Samaritan woman at a well.
passages.en: Jesus says to her, “Believe me, woman, that an hour is coming when you will worship the Father neither on this mountain nor in Jerusalem.”

rows.note: λέγει, dīcit.
αὐτῇ: to her, feminine. Latin eī serves for him or her.
ὁ Ἰησοῦς, Jēsūs.
πίστευε: believe, an imperative of πιστεύω. Latin: crēde.
μοι: me, in the dative, as πιστεύω requires. Latin too: mihi.
γύναι: woman, the vocative, used to address her. Latin puts it first: mulier.
ὅτι: that. quia.
ἔρχεται: is coming. venit.
ὥρα: an hour, a time. Latin: hōra.
ὅτε: when. Latin: quandō.
οὔτε: neither. A second οὔτε will follow, meaning nor. Latin: neque, then neque again.
ἐν τῷ ὄρει τούτῳ: on this mountain, from ὄρος. Latin: in monte hōc.
οὔτε: nor. neque.
ἐν Ἱεροσολύμοις: in Jerusalem, a plural form in Greek. Latin too: in Jerosolymīs.
προσκυνήσετε: you will worship, from προσκυνέω, to bow down, to worship. A future, plural. Latin: adōrābitis, from adōrō.
τῷ πατρί: the Father, in the dative, which προσκυνέω often takes. Latin: Patrem, accusative.

passages.ctx: Jesus has told the disciples he has food they know nothing of.
passages.en: So the disciples were saying to each other, “Surely no one brought him anything to eat?”

rows.note: ἔλεγον: they were saying, the imperfect. Latin also: dīcēbant.
οὖν: so. ergō.
οἱ μαθηταί: the disciples. discipulī.
πρὸς ἀλλήλους: to one another, from ἀλλήλων, which has no nominative. Latin: ad invicem, in turn.
μή: here it opens a question expecting the answer no. Latin: numquid, which does the same.
τις: anyone. Latin: aliquis, someone.
ἤνεγκεν: brought, an aorist of φέρω, from another stem. Latin: attulit, the perfect of afferō, to bring.
αὐτῷ: him, eī.
φαγεῖν: to eat, an aorist infinitive of ἐσθίω, again another stem. Latin: mandūcāre, from mandūcō, to chew.

passages.ctx: At the pool, Jesus speaks to a man ill for thirty-eight years.
passages.en: Jesus says to him, “Rise, lift up your mat, and walk about.”

rows.note: λέγει, dīcit.
αὐτῷ, eī.
ὁ Ἰησοῦς, Jēsūs.
ἔγειρε: rise, the imperative of ἐγείρω. Latin: surge.
ἆρον: lift up, an aorist imperative of αἴρω. Latin: tolle, from tollō, to lift or take away.
τὸν κράβαττον: the mat, a poor man’s pallet. Latin borrows it: grabātum.
σου: your. Latin, tuum.
καί, et.
περιπάτει: walk about, from περιπατέω, to walk around. The present imperative suits an ongoing action. Latin: ambulā, from ambulō, to walk.

nl.m: lift up, raise; take away, remove

passages.ctx: Jesus has healed a man on the Sabbath.
passages.en: And because of this the Jews were hounding Jesus, since he was doing these things on a Sabbath.

rows.note: καί: and. Latin leaves it out.
διὰ τοῦτο: because of this. Latin uses one word, proptereā.
ἐδίωκον: they were hounding, from διώκω, to pursue or persecute. The imperfect, an ongoing action. Latin: persequēbantur, from persequor, passive in form but active in meaning.
οἱ Ἰουδαῖοι: the Jews. Jūdaeī.
τὸν Ἰησοῦν: Jesus, the object. Jēsum.
ὅτι, quia.
ταῦτα: these things, neuter plural. haec.
ἐποίει: he was doing, the imperfect. Latin: faciēbat.
ἐν σαββάτῳ: on a Sabbath, from σάββατον, the day of rest. Latin borrows it: in sabbatō, from sabbatum.

passages.ctx: Jesus has asked Philip where to buy bread for the crowd.
passages.en: Now he was saying this to put him to the test, for he himself knew what he was about to do.

rows.note: τοῦτο, hoc: this.
δέ, autem.
ἔλεγεν, dīcēbat: he was saying.
πειράζων: testing, from πειράζω, to test. Latin: tentāns, from temptō.
αὐτόν: him, Philip. Latin: eum.
αὐτός: he himself. Latin: ipse.
γάρ, enim: for.
ᾔδει: he knew, a past form of οἶδα. Latin: sciēbat.
τί, quid: what.
ἔμελλεν: he was about to, from μέλλω. Latin instead uses esset with a future participle.
ποιεῖν: to do. Latin: factūrus, going to do.

passages.ctx: Jesus has come to Jerusalem for the Festival of Booths.
passages.en: Now, with the feast already half over, Jesus went up into the temple and was teaching.

rows.note: ἤδη: already. Latin: jam.
δέ, autem.
τῆς ἑορτῆς: the feast. Latin says the feast day: diē fēstō.
μεσούσης: being at its middle, a participle of μεσόω. With the noun it forms a genitive absolute, a clause set apart. Latin uses an ablative absolute: mediante, from mediō.
ἀνέβη: went up, the aorist of ἀναβαίνω, to go up. Latin: ascendit, from ascendō.
Ἰησοῦς, Jēsūs.
εἰς τὸ ἱερόν: into the temple. ἱερόν is the neuter of ἱερός, holy, so the holy place, the whole temple area. Latin: in templum.
καί, et.
ἐδίδασκεν: he was teaching, the imperfect. Latin: docēbat.

passages.ctx: Jesus answers those who accuse him.
passages.en: But I am not seeking my own glory; there is one who seeks it and who judges.

rows.note: ἐγώ: I, stated for emphasis. ego.
δέ, autem.
οὐ, nōn.
ζητῶ: I seek, from ζητέω. Latin: quaerō.
τὴν δόξαν: the glory, from δόξα, glory, honor, a good name. Latin: glōriam, from glōria.
μου: of me, so my. Latin uses the adjective meam, agreeing with glōriam.
ἔστιν: there is. est.
ὁ ζητῶν: the one seeking, a participle with the article. Latin uses a clause: quī quaerat, one who seeks, in the subjunctive.
καί, et.
κρίνων: judging, from κρίνω, to judge. It shares the one article. Latin: jūdicet, from jūdicō, to judge, again subjunctive.

passages.en: Amen, amen, I tell you, if someone keeps my word, he will never look on death, to the end of time.

rows.note: ἀμήν: amen, truly. A Hebrew word, kept in Greek and Latin: āmēn.
Doubled for weight: ἀμήν, āmēn.
λέγω: I say. dīcō.
ὑμῖν: to you, plural. vōbīs.
ἐάν: if, with the subjunctive. Latin: sī.
τις: someone. quis.
τὸν ἐμόν: my, the adjective ἐμός. Latin: meum.
λόγον: word, from λόγος, word or message. Latin: sermōnem, from sermō, speech.
τηρήσῃ: keeps, from τηρέω, to keep or guard. An aorist subjunctive after ἐάν. Latin: servāverit, the future perfect of servō: will have kept.
θάνατον: death. Latin: mortem, from mors.
οὐ μή: two negatives together, a strong never. Latin has just nōn.
θεωρήσῃ: he will look on, an aorist subjunctive of θεωρέω. With οὐ μή it acts as a strong future. Latin: vidēbit, a plain future.
εἰς τὸν αἰῶνα: into the age, so forever. αἰών means an age. Latin: in aeternum, into the eternal, from aeternus.

passages.ctx: Neighbours question the man who was born blind.
passages.en: And they said to him, “Where is that man?” He says, “I do not know.”

rows.note: καί, et.
εἶπαν: they said. dīxērunt.
αὐτῷ: to him. eī.
ποῦ: where, a question word. Latin: ubi.
ἐστιν, est.
ἐκεῖνος: that man. ille.
λέγει: he says. ait.
οὐκ οἶδα: I do not know. οἶδα is a perfect form with a present meaning. Latin uses one word: nesciō, I do not know.

passages.ctx: Some Pharisees ask Jesus whether they too are blind.
passages.en: Jesus said to them, “If you were blind, you would not have sin; but now you say, ‘We see.’ Your sin remains.”

rows.note: εἶπεν, dīxit.
αὐτοῖς, eīs.
ὁ Ἰησοῦς, Jēsūs.
εἰ: if. Here it begins a condition contrary to fact: if you were, but you are not. Latin: sī.
τυφλοί: blind, from τυφλός. Latin: caecī, from caecus, blind.
ἦτε: you were, the imperfect of εἰμί. Latin uses the subjunctive: essētis.
οὐκ, nōn.
ἄν: a small particle with no English word of its own. Here it marks the result as unreal: would. Latin leaves it out, and the subjunctive does the work.
εἴχετε: you would have, the imperfect of ἔχω. Latin: habērētis, the imperfect subjunctive of habeō.
ἁμαρτίαν: sin, from ἁμαρτία. Latin: peccātum, a noun from peccō, to sin.
νῦν: now. Latin: nunc.
δέ: but. Latin: vērō, but indeed.
λέγετε: you say. dīcitis.
ὅτι here only marks a quotation, so English skips it. Latin copies it with quia.
βλέπομεν: we see, from βλέπω. Latin: vidēmus.
ἡ ἁμαρτία: the sin, now the subject. peccātum.
ὑμῶν: of you, so your. Latin uses the adjective vestrum.
μένει: remains, from μένω, to stay. Latin: manet, from maneō, to remain.

passages.ctx: Some say Jesus has a demon, but others disagree.
passages.en: Others were saying, “These words are not those of a demon-possessed man. Surely a demon cannot open the eyes of the blind?”

rows.note: ἄλλοι: others, from ἄλλος, other or another. Latin: aliī, from alius.
ἔλεγον, dīcēbant: they were saying.
ταῦτα τὰ ῥήματα: these words. Latin: haec verba.
οὐκ ἔστιν: are not. Greek pairs a neuter plural subject with a singular verb. Latin says nōn sunt, plural.
δαιμονιζομένου: of one possessed by a demon, from δαιμονίζομαι. A genitive participle. Latin: daemonium habentis, of one having a demon.
μή opens a question expecting the answer no. Latin: numquid.
δαιμόνιον: a demon. Latin simply borrows it: daemonium.
δύναται: can. Latin: potest.
τυφλῶν: of the blind. Latin: caecōrum.
ὀφθαλμούς: eyes. Latin: oculōs.
ἀνοῖξαι: to open, an aorist infinitive of ἀνοίγω. Latin: aperīre, from aperiō.

passages.ctx: Martha speaks with Jesus after the death of her brother Lazarus.
passages.en: Martha says to him, “I know that he will rise at the resurrection, on the final day.”

rows.note: λέγει, dīcit: says.
αὐτῷ, eī: to him.
ἡ Μάρθα: Martha. Greek often puts the article before a name. Latin cannot: Martha.
οἶδα: I know, perfect in form but present in meaning. Latin: sciō.
ὅτι, quia: that.
ἀναστήσεται: he will rise, the future middle of ἀνίστημι, to raise or to rise. Latin: resurget, from resurgō.
ἐν τῇ ἀναστάσει: at the resurrection, from ἀνάστασις, the noun of the same verb. Latin: in resurrectiōne, from resurrectiō.
ἐν τῇ ἐσχάτῃ ἡμέρᾳ: on the final day. Latin: in novissimō diē, in the newest day, a superlative of novus.

passages.ctx: At the Last Supper, Jesus speaks to his disciples.
