passages.en: Little children, I am still with you for a little while. You will look for me, and just as I said to the Jews, ‘Where I am going, you cannot come,’ now I say to you as well.

rows.note: τεκνία: little children, from τεκνίον, a diminutive of child. Latin has its own diminutive: fīliolī, little sons.
ἔτι: still. Latin: adhūc.
μικρόν: a little, from μικρός, small. The neuter here means a little while. Latin: modicum, from modicus.
μεθ’ ὑμῶν: with you. Latin makes one word: vōbīscum.
εἰμί, sum: I am.
ζητήσετε: you will look for, a future. Latin: quaerētis.
με, mē.
καί, et.
καθώς, sīcut: just as.
εἶπον: I said. Latin: dīxī.
τοῖς Ἰουδαίοις: to the Jews. Latin: Jūdaeīs.
ὅτι here only introduces a quotation. Latin leaves it out.
ὅπου: where. Latin: quō, to where, because there is motion.
ἐγώ, ego: I, for emphasis.
ὑπάγω: I am going away, I depart. Latin: vādō, I go.
ὑμεῖς, vōs: you.
οὐ δύνασθε: you cannot. Latin: nōn potestis.
ἐλθεῖν, venīre: to come.
καί here means also. Latin: et.
ὑμῖν, vōbīs: to you.
λέγω, dīcō: I say.
ἄρτι: now, at this moment. Latin: modo, just now.

passages.en: I am giving you a new command, that you love one another: just as I loved you, that you too love one another.

rows.note: ἐντολήν: a command, from ἐντολή. Latin: mandātum, a thing commanded, from mandō, to entrust or command.
καινήν: new, from καινός, feminine to match the noun. Latin: novum, neuter to match mandātum.
δίδωμι: I give. Latin: dō.
ὑμῖν, vōbīs: to you.
ἵνα, ut: that.
ἀγαπᾶτε: you love, from ἀγαπάω, to love. It is subjunctive after ἵνα. Latin: dīligātis, also subjunctive, from dīligō.
ἀλλήλους: one another. Latin uses an adverb, invicem, mutually.
καθώς, sīcut: just as.
ἠγάπησα: I loved, an aorist. Latin: dīlēxī, a perfect.
ὑμᾶς, vōs: you, now the object.
ἵνα, ut: that.
καί: also. Latin: et.
ὑμεῖς, vōs: you.
ἀγαπᾶτε ἀλλήλους, dīligātis invicem: love one another.

passages.ctx: At the Last Supper, Jesus speaks to his disciples.
passages.en: I leave you peace; I give you my peace. I do not give to you in the way the world gives. Let your heart not be troubled, nor let it lose courage.

rows.note: εἰρήνην: peace, from εἰρήνη. Latin: pācem, from pāx.
ἀφίημι: I leave. The same verb can mean let go or forgive. Latin: relinquō, I leave behind.
ὑμῖν, vōbīs: to you.
εἰρήνην, pācem: peace again.
τὴν ἐμήν: my, literally the my, after the noun. Latin: meam.
δίδωμι, dō: I give.
ὑμῖν, vōbīs.
οὐ, nōn: not.
καθώς: as. Here Latin says quōmodo, in what way.
ὁ κόσμος: the world. Both κόσμος and mundus can also mean adornment.
δίδωσιν: gives. Latin: dat.
ἐγώ, ego: I, with emphasis.
δίδωμι, dō.
ὑμῖν, vōbīs.
μή: not, the negative for commands. Latin: nōn.
ταρασσέσθω: let it be troubled, from ταράσσω, to stir up. A third person imperative, so English needs let. Latin uses a subjunctive: turbētur, from turbō.
ὑμῶν: of you, your. Latin uses the adjective vestrum, agreeing with cor.
ἡ καρδία: the heart. Latin: cor.
μηδέ: and not, nor. Latin: neque.
δειλιάτω: let it lose courage, from δειλιάω, to be timid. Latin: formīdet, from formīdō, to dread.

passages.ctx: Jesus tells his disciples that he is going away.
passages.en: And now I have told you before it occurs, so that whenever it occurs, you may believe.

rows.note: καί, et.
νῦν, nunc: now.
εἴρηκα: I have told, perfect of λέγω. Latin: dīxī.
ὑμῖν, vōbīs.
πρίν: before. Latin: priusquam.
γενέσθαι: to happen. Latin uses a subjunctive, fīat.
ἵνα, ut: so that.
ὅταν: whenever, from ὅτε, when, and ἄν. Latin: cum.
γένηται: it happens, a subjunctive. Latin: factum fuerit, it will have happened.
πιστεύσητε: you may believe. Latin: crēdātis.

passages.ctx: Peter is asked a third time whether he is a disciple.
passages.en: So Peter denied it once more, and right away a rooster crowed.

rows.note: πάλιν: again. iterum.
οὖν: so. ergō.
ἠρνήσατο: he denied, the aorist of ἀρνέομαι, to deny. Latin: negāvit, a perfect, from negō.
Πέτρος, Petrus: Peter.
καί, et.
εὐθέως: immediately. Latin: statim.
ἀλέκτωρ: a rooster. Latin: gallus.
ἐφώνησεν: crowed, from φωνέω, to make a sound or call. It is related to φωνή, voice. Latin: cantāvit, sang, from cantō.

passages.ctx: The chief priests ask Pilate to change the sign on the cross.
passages.en: Pilate replied, “What I have written, I have written.”

rows.note: ἀπεκρίθη: he answered. respondit.
ὁ Πιλᾶτος: Pilate. Pīlātus.
ὅ: what, the neuter of ὅς. Latin: quod.
γέγραφα: I have written, the perfect of γράφω, to write. The perfect means the writing stands. Latin: scrīpsī, from scrībō.
Again: γέγραφα, scrīpsī.

passages.ctx: Peter is travelling among the believers.
passages.en: Now it came about that Peter, while passing through every place, also came down to the saints living in Lydda.

rows.note: ἐγένετο: it came about. Latin: factum est.
δέ, autem: now.
Πέτρον: Peter, accusative, subject of the infinitive. Latin uses an ut clause instead, so Petrus is nominative.
διερχόμενον: passing through. Latin: dum pertrānsīret, while he passed through.
διὰ πάντων: through all. Latin puts through into the verb’s prefix, and all is ūniversōs, from ūniversus.
κατελθεῖν: to come down, from κατέρχομαι. Latin: dēvenīret, from dēveniō.
καί: also. Latin leaves it out.
πρός, ad: to.
τοὺς ἁγίους: the saints, from ἅγιος, holy. Latin: sanctōs, from sanctus.
τοὺς κατοικοῦντας: the ones dwelling, from κατοικέω. Latin: quī habitābant, who lived, from habitō.
Λύδδα: Lydda. Latin: Lyddae, the locative, at Lydda.

passages.ctx: Paul, preaching in a synagogue, has just spoken of King David.
passages.en: From this man’s seed God, as promised, brought Israel a Saviour, Jesus, after John had first proclaimed, ahead of his coming, a baptism of repentance to all the people of Israel.

rows.note: τούτου: of this one, placed first for emphasis. Latin keeps it first: hujus.
ὁ θεός, Deus: God.
ἀπὸ τοῦ σπέρματος: from the seed. σπέρμα means seed, and so descendants. Latin: ex sēmine, from sēmen.
κατ’ ἐπαγγελίαν: according to promise, from ἐπαγγελία, a promise. Latin: secundum prōmissiōnem.
ἤγαγεν: he brought, from ἄγω. Latin: ēdūxit, he led out, from ēdūcō.
τῷ Ἰσραήλ: to Israel. The name never changes, so the article shows the dative. Latin: Isrāēl.
σωτῆρα: a saviour, from σωτήρ. Latin: salvātōrem, from salvātor.
Ἰησοῦν, Jēsum: Jesus.
προκηρύξαντος: having proclaimed beforehand, from προκηρύσσω. A genitive absolute, a phrase standing apart from the main sentence. Latin uses an ablative absolute: praedicante.
Ἰωάννου: John, genitive. Latin: Jōanne, ablative.
πρό: before. Latin: ante.
προσώπου: face, from πρόσωπον. Before the face of is a Hebrew idiom for ahead of. Latin: faciem, from faciēs.
τῆς εἰσόδου: of the entrance, from εἴσοδος, a way in. Latin: adventūs, of the coming.
αὐτοῦ, ejus: his.
βάπτισμα: a baptism. Latin borrows it: baptismum.
μετανοίας: of repentance, a change of mind. Latin: poenitentiae.
παντί: to all, dative. Latin: omnī.
τῷ λαῷ: the people, from λαός. Latin: populō, from populus, also dative.
Ἰσραήλ: of Israel, now a genitive. Latin: Isrāēl.

passages.ctx: Paul meets disciples in Ephesus who knew only John’s baptism.
passages.en: Having heard this, they were baptized into the name of the Lord Jesus; and after Paul laid hands on them, the Holy Spirit came upon them, and they were speaking in tongues and prophesying.

rows.note: ἀκούσαντες δέ: and having heard, from ἀκούω. Latin: hīs audītīs, these things heard, an ablative absolute.
ἐβαπτίσθησαν: they were baptized, an aorist passive of βαπτίζω, to dip, to baptize. Latin: baptīzātī sunt, from baptīzō.
εἰς τὸ ὄνομα: into the name. Latin says in nōmine, in the name, from nōmen.
τοῦ κυρίου Ἰησοῦ: of the Lord Jesus, genitives. Latin: Dominī Jēsū.
καί, et.
ἐπιθέντος: having laid on, from ἐπιτίθημι, in a genitive absolute, a phrase set apart from the main clause. Latin: cum imposuisset, when he had laid on, from impōnō.
αὐτοῖς: on them, a dative. Latin: illīs.
τοῦ Παύλου: Paul, genitive as the participle’s subject. Latin has a plain nominative: Paulus.
χεῖρας: hands, from χείρ. Latin: manūs.
ἦλθε: came. Latin: vēnit.
τὸ πνεῦμα τὸ ἅγιον: the Holy Spirit, with the article repeated. Latin: Spīritus Sānctus.
ἐπ’ αὐτούς: upon them. Latin: super eōs.
ἐλάλουν: they were speaking, from λαλέω, to speak, an imperfect, ongoing past action. Latin: loquēbantur, from loquor, a deponent, passive in form, active in meaning.
τε: and, a light word never placed first. Latin puts et before the verb.
γλώσσαις: in tongues, from γλῶσσα, tongue, language. Latin: linguīs, ablative, from lingua.
καί, et.
ἐπροφήτευον: they were prophesying, from προφητεύω. Latin: prophētābant, from prophētō.

passages.ctx: Paul writes to the church in Rome.
passages.en: Or are you unaware, brothers, for I speak to people who know law, that the law is master of a person for as much time as he lives?

rows.note: ἤ: or, opening a question. Latin: an, also a question word.
ἀγνοεῖτε: are you unaware, from ἀγνοέω. Latin: ignōrātis, from ignōrō, source of our ignore.
ἀδελφοί: brothers, from ἀδελφός, in the vocative, for addressing someone. Latin: frātrēs, from frāter.
γινώσκουσιν: to people who know, a dative participle. Latin matches it: scientibus, from sciō.
γάρ: for. Latin: enim.
νόμον: law, from νόμος, with no article. Latin: lēgem, from lēx.
λαλῶ: I speak, from λαλέω. Latin: loquor.
ὅτι: that. Latin: quia.
ὁ νόμος: the law, now the subject. Latin: lēx.
κυριεύει: is master, from κυριεύω, related to κύριος, lord. Latin: dominātur, from dominor, related to dominus.
τοῦ ἀνθρώπου: of a person, genitive after this verb. Latin: in homine, in a person.

rows.gg: as much as, as great as
rows.note: ἐφ’ ὅσον: for as much, from ὅσος. Latin: quantō, from quantus, with no preposition.
χρόνον: time, from χρόνος; with ἐπί, an accusative of how long. Latin: tempore, ablative, from tempus.
ζῇ: he lives, from ζάω, to live. Latin: vīvit, from vīvō.

ng.m: as much as, as many as

nl.m: how great, how much; as great as

passages.ctx: Paul sends greetings to friends in Rome.
passages.en: Greet Rufus, the chosen one in the Lord, and his mother and mine.

rows.note: ἀσπάσασθε: greet, an aorist imperative of ἀσπάζομαι. Latin: salūtāte, from salūtō.
Ῥοῦφον: Rufus, a Latin name in Greek letters. Latin: Rūfum.
τὸν ἐκλεκτόν: the chosen one, from ἐκλεκτός, chosen. Latin has no article: ēlectum, chosen, from ēligō, to choose.
ἐν κυρίῳ: in the Lord. Latin: in Dominō.
καί, et.
τὴν μητέρα: the mother, from μήτηρ. Latin: mātrem, from māter.
αὐτοῦ: his. Latin: ejus.
καί, et.
ἐμοῦ: of me, mine. Greek uses the genitive of the pronoun. Latin uses the adjective meam, agreeing with mother.

passages.ctx: Paul writes about spiritual gifts in worship.
passages.en: So you too, since you are eager for spirits, seek that you may abound for the building up of the church.

rows.note: οὕτως: so. Latin: sīc, so, thus.
καί: also, too. Latin: et.
ὑμεῖς: you, plural. Latin: vōs.
ἐπεί: since. Latin: quoniam.
ζηλωταί: zealots, eager ones, from ζηλωτής. Latin: aemulātōrēs, rivals, from aemulātor.
ἐστε: you are. Latin: estis.
πνευμάτων: of spirits, a genitive plural. Latin: spīrituum.
πρὸς τὴν οἰκοδομήν: for the building up, from οἰκοδομή. Latin: ad aedificātiōnem, from aedificātiō.
τῆς ἐκκλησίας: of the church, from ἐκκλησία, assembly, church. Latin borrows it: ecclēsiae, from ecclēsia.
ζητεῖτε: seek, a command. Latin: quaerite.
ἵνα: that. Latin: ut.
περισσεύητε: you may abound, from περισσεύω, a subjunctive after ἵνα. Latin: abundētis, from abundō, also subjunctive.

passages.ctx: Paul answers rivals who boast about themselves.
passages.en: Since many are boasting by the standard of the flesh, I also will boast.

rows.note: ἐπεί: since. Latin: quoniam.
πολλοί: many, from πολύς, much, many. Latin: multī, from multus.
καυχῶνται: they boast, from καυχάομαι, to boast, a middle verb. Latin: glōriantur, from glōrior, a deponent.
κατὰ σάρκα: according to the flesh, by its standard, from σάρξ, flesh. Latin: secundum carnem, from carō, flesh.
κἀγώ: I also, a blend of καί and ἐγώ. Latin keeps the two words apart: et ego.
καυχήσομαι: I will boast, the future. Latin: glōriābor, also future.

ng.m: and I, I too, even I

passages.ctx: Paul defends his message to the Galatians.
passages.en: For am I now persuading people, or God? Or am I seeking to please people? If I were still pleasing people, I would not be Christ’s slave.

rows.note: ἄρτι: now. Latin: modo, just now.
γάρ, enim: for.
ἀνθρώπους: people. Latin: hominibus, a dative, which its verb requires.
πείθω: I persuade, also its dictionary form. Here, am I trying to persuade. Latin: suādeō.
ἤ: or. Latin: an.
τὸν θεόν: God. Latin again a dative: Deō.
ἤ, an: or.
ζητῶ: am I seeking. Latin: quaerō.
ἀνθρώποις: people, now dative after the next verb. Latin: hominibus.
ἀρέσκειν: to please, from ἀρέσκω. Latin: placēre, from placeō.
εἰ: if. Latin: sī.
ἔτι: still. Latin: adhūc.
ἀνθρώποις, hominibus: people.
ἤρεσκον: I was pleasing, an imperfect, here contrary to fact. Latin: placērem, an imperfect subjunctive.
Χριστοῦ: of Christ, from Χριστός, anointed. Latin: Chrīstī, from Chrīstus.
δοῦλος: slave. Latin: servus.
οὐκ, nōn: not.
ἂν ἤμην: I would be. ἄν marks the unreal result. Latin uses the subjunctive essem.

passages.ctx: Paul questions the Galatians about how they received the Spirit.
passages.en: So the one who supplies you with the Spirit and works miracles among you: is it from works of law, or from the hearing of faith?

rows.note: ὁ: the one, the article with a participle. Latin uses quī, who, with ordinary verbs.
οὖν, ergō: so.
ἐπιχορηγῶν: supplying, from ἐπιχορηγέω. Latin: tribuit, he grants, from tribuō.
ὑμῖν: to you. Latin: vōbīs.
τὸ πνεῦμα: the Spirit. Latin: Spīritum.
καί, et.
ἐνεργῶν: working, from ἐνεργέω, source of our energy. Latin: operātur, from operor, a deponent.
δυνάμεις: powers, miracles, from δύναμις. Latin: virtūtēs.
ἐν ὑμῖν: among you. Latin: in vōbīs.
ἐξ ἔργων: from works, from ἔργον, work, deed. Latin: ex operibus, from opus, work.
νόμου: of law. Latin: lēgis.
ἤ: or. Latin: an.
ἐξ ἀκοῆς: from hearing, from ἀκοή, hearing, report. Latin: ex audītū, from the noun audītus.
πίστεως: of faith. Latin: fideī.

passages.ctx: Paul worries about the Galatians.
passages.en: I am afraid for you, that I have somehow toiled over you for nothing.

rows.note: φοβοῦμαι: I am afraid, from φοβέομαι, to fear. Latin: timeō, I fear.
ὑμᾶς, vōs: you.
μή: that, after a verb of fearing. Latin: nē, the same idiom.
πως: somehow. Latin: forte, by chance.
εἰκῇ: for nothing. Latin: sine causā, without cause, from sine, without.
κεκοπίακα: I have toiled, a perfect of κοπιάω, to toil. Latin: labōrāverim, perfect subjunctive after nē.
εἰς ὑμᾶς: over you. Latin: in vōbīs.

passages.ctx: Paul writes to the Galatians.
passages.en: For we, by the Spirit, from faith, eagerly await the hope of righteousness.

rows.note: ἡμεῖς: we, stressed. Latin: nōs.
γάρ, enim: for.
πνεύματι: by the Spirit, a dative. Latin: spīritū, ablative.
ἐκ πίστεως: from faith. Latin: ex fidē.
ἐλπίδα: hope, from ἐλπίς. Latin: spem, from spēs.
δικαιοσύνης: of righteousness, from δικαιοσύνη, righteousness, justice. Latin: jūstitiae, from jūstitia.
ἀπεκδεχόμεθα: we eagerly await, from ἀπεκδέχομαι, a verb with two prefixes. Latin: exspectāmus, from exspectō.

passages.ctx: Paul writes from prison to the Ephesians.
passages.en: For this reason I ask you not to be discouraged at my afflictions for your sake, which is your glory.

rows.note: διό: therefore, for this reason. Latin: propter quod, because of which, from propter, because of.
αἰτοῦμαι: I ask, from αἰτέω, to ask, here in the middle voice. Latin: petō, I ask, I seek.
μή: not. Latin: nē.
ἐγκακεῖν: to lose heart, be discouraged, from ἐγκακέω, an infinitive. Latin makes a clause: nē dēficiātis, that you not fail, from dēficiō.
ἐν ταῖς θλίψεσίν: in the afflictions, from θλῖψις, pressure, affliction. Latin: in trībulātiōnibus, from trībulātiō.
μου: my. Latin: meīs.
ὑπὲρ ὑμῶν: for you, on your behalf, from ὑπέρ, for, over, here with the genitive. Latin: prō vōbīs.
ἥτις: which. Latin: quae.
ἐστίν, est: is.
δόξα: glory. Latin: glōria.
ὑμῶν: your. Latin: vestra, an adjective.

nl.m: because of,on account of; for the sake of

passages.ctx: Paul commends Timothy to the Philippians.
passages.en: But you know his tested worth, that like a child to a father he served alongside me for the gospel.

rows.note: τὴν δὲ δοκιμήν: but the proof, tested worth, from δοκιμή. Latin: experīmentum autem.
αὐτοῦ: his. Latin: ejus.
γινώσκετε: you know. Latin reads it as a command: cognōscite, know. The Greek allows both.
ὅτι: that. Latin: quia.
ὡς: as. Latin: sīcut.
πατρί: to a father, a dative. Latin: patrī.
τέκνον: child, a neuter noun. Latin says fīlius, son.
σὺν ἐμοί: with me, from σύν, taking the dative. Latin: mēcum, with the pronoun before cum.
ἐδούλευσεν: he served as a slave, from δουλεύω, akin to δοῦλος. Latin: servīvit, from serviō, akin to servus.
εἰς τὸ εὐαγγέλιον: for the gospel. Latin: in Ēvangeliō, in the gospel.

nl.m: serve, be a slave to (+ dat.)

passages.ctx: Paul writes to the church in Philippi.
passages.en: Be glad in the Lord at all times. Again I will say: be glad.

rows.note: Χαίρετε: be glad, rejoice, a command to many. Latin: gaudēte.
ἐν κυρίῳ, in Dominō: in the Lord.
πάντοτε: always. Latin: semper, always.
πάλιν, iterum: again.
ἐρῶ: I will say, the future of λέγω. Latin keeps the present: dīcō.
χαίρετε, gaudēte.

passages.ctx: Paul writes to the church in Thessalonica.
passages.en: Therefore, brothers, stand firm, and hold fast to the traditions which you were taught, whether through spoken word or through our letter.

rows.note: ἄρα οὖν: therefore, so then. ἄρα draws a conclusion, and οὖν adds to it. Latin uses one word: itaque, and so.
ἀδελφοί: brothers. Latin: frātrēs.
στήκετε: stand firm, from στήκω. Latin: stāte, from stō.
καὶ, et.
κρατεῖτε: hold fast, from κρατέω, to grasp, to hold fast. Latin: tenēte, from teneō, to hold.
τὰς παραδόσεις: the traditions, from παράδοσις, something handed on. Latin: trāditiōnēs.
ἃς: which. Latin: quās.
ἐδιδάχθητε: you were taught, an aorist passive of διδάσκω. Latin turns it round: didicistis, you learned, from discō.
εἴτε: whether. Paired, it means whether this or that. Latin pairs sīve the same way.
διὰ λόγου: through word, that is, by speech. Latin: per sermōnem.
εἴτε, sīve: or.
δι’ ἐπιστολῆς ἡμῶν: through our letter, from ἐπιστολή. Latin: per epistolam nostram.

nl.m: or if; sīve … sīve whether … or

passages.ctx: Paul gives Timothy instructions about prayer.
passages.en: So I want the men to pray in every place, raising holy hands without anger and dispute.

rows.note: Βούλομαι: I want. Middle in form, active in meaning. Latin: volō.
οὖν: so. Latin: ergō.
προσεύχεσθαι: to pray, an infinitive of προσεύχομαι. Latin: ōrāre, from ōrō.
τοὺς ἄνδρας: the men, from ἀνήρ, a man or husband. Accusative, as the subject of the infinitive. Latin: virōs, from vir.
ἐν παντὶ, in omnī: in every.
τόπῳ: place, from τόπος. Latin: locō, from locus.
ἐπαίροντας: raising, a participle of ἐπαίρω, to lift up. Latin: levantēs.
ὁσίους: holy, from ὅσιος. It looks masculine, but describes the feminine hands. Latin says pūrās, pure.
χεῖρας: hands. Latin: manūs.
χωρὶς: without, with the genitive. Latin: sine, with the ablative.
ὀργῆς: anger, from ὀργή. Latin: īrā, from īra.
καὶ, et.
διαλογισμοῦ: dispute, from διαλογισμός, reasoning or argument. Latin: disceptātiōne.

passages.ctx: Paul instructs Timothy about charges brought against elders.
passages.en: Do not accept an accusation against an elder unless it rests on two or three witnesses. Those who keep sinning, rebuke before everyone, so that the rest also may have fear.

rows.note: κατὰ: against, with the genitive. Latin: adversus, against, with the accusative.
πρεσβυτέρου: an elder. Latin borrows the Greek word: presbyterum.
κατηγορίαν: accusation, from κατηγορία. Latin: accūsātiōnem.
μὴ παραδέχου: do not accept, from παραδέχομαι, to receive. Latin forbids with nōlī and an infinitive: nōlī recipere, literally be unwilling to receive.
ἐκτὸς εἰ μὴ: unless, literally outside if not. Latin: nisi.
ἐπὶ: on, here on the basis of. Latin: sub, under.
δύο: two, which rarely changes its ending. Latin: duōbus, from duo, ablative after sub.
ἢ: or. Latin: aut.
τριῶν: three. Latin: tribus.
μαρτύρων: witnesses, from μάρτυς, whence martyr. Latin: testibus, from testis.
τοὺς ἁμαρτάνοντας: those who are sinning, from ἁμαρτάνω, to sin. The article with a participle makes a noun. Latin uses the participle alone: peccantēs, from peccō.
ἐνώπιον: before, in front of, with the genitive. Latin: cōram, in the presence of.
πάντων: all. Latin: omnibus.
ἔλεγχε: rebuke, from ἐλέγχω, to expose or reprove. A command to one person. Latin: argue, from arguō.
ἵνα: so that. Latin: ut.
καὶ: also. Latin: et.
οἱ λοιποὶ: the rest, from λοιπός, remaining. Latin: cēterī, the others, from cēterus.
φόβον: fear, from φόβος, whence our word phobia. Latin: timōrem, from timor.
ἔχωσιν: they may have, a subjunctive after ἵνα. Latin likewise: habeant.

passages.ctx: The writer explains how a high priest is appointed.
passages.en: And no one takes the honour upon himself; rather, he is called by God, just as Aaron too was.

rows.note: καὶ οὐχ: and not. Latin uses one word: nec.
ἑαυτῷ: to himself, a dative. Latin: sibi.
τις: anyone; with the negative, no one. Latin: quisquam, used after a negative.
λαμβάνει: he takes. Latin: sūmit, from sūmō, to take up.
τὴν τιμήν: the honor, from τιμή, honor or price. Latin: honōrem, from honor.
ἀλλὰ, sed: but.
καλούμενος: being called, a passive participle of καλέω, to call. Latin uses a clause: quī vocātur, who is called, from vocō.
ὑπὸ τοῦ θεοῦ: by God, with ὑπό naming the doer. Latin: ā Deō.
καθώσπερ: just as. Latin: tamquam.
καὶ: also. Latin leaves it out.
Ἀαρών: Aaron, a Hebrew name with no endings. Latin: Aarōn.

passages.ctx: The writer compares Abraham with the priest Melchizedek.
passages.en: Now, with no dispute at all, the lesser one is blessed by the better one.

rows.note: χωρὶς, sine: without.
δὲ, autem.
πάσης: all, here any. Latin: ūllā, any.
ἀντιλογίας: dispute, from ἀντιλογία, a speaking against. Latin: contrādictiōne.
τὸ ἔλαττον: the lesser, from ἐλάσσων. Latin: quod minus est, what is less.
ὑπὸ τοῦ κρείττονος: by the better, from κρείττων. Latin: ā meliōre.
εὐλογεῖται: is blessed, from εὐλογέω, to speak well of. Latin: benedīcitur, from benedīcō.

passages.ctx: The writer warns his readers about deliberate sin.
passages.en: For when we keep sinning by choice after receiving the full knowledge of the truth, there is no longer any sacrifice left for sins, but a certain dreadful expectation of judgment, and a zeal of fire that is about to devour the opponents.

rows.note: Ἑκουσίως: by choice. Latin: voluntāriē.
γὰρ, enim: for.
ἁμαρτανόντων ἡμῶν: we sinning, a genitive absolute, a phrase set apart from the main clause. Latin has the ablative absolute: peccantibus nōbīs.
μετὰ: after, with the accusative. Latin: post.
τὸ λαβεῖν: the receiving, an infinitive used as a noun. Latin has a participle: acceptam.
τὴν ἐπίγνωσιν: the full knowledge, from ἐπίγνωσις. Latin: nōtitiam.
τῆς ἀληθείας: of the truth, from ἀλήθεια. Latin: vēritātis, from vēritās.
οὐκέτι: no longer. Latin: jam nōn.
περὶ ἁμαρτιῶν: for sins. Latin: prō peccātīs.
ἀπολείπεται: is left, from ἀπολείπω. Latin: relinquitur.
θυσία: a sacrifice. Latin: hostia, a victim.
φοβερὰ: dreadful, from φοβερός, akin to φόβος, fear. Latin: terribilis.
δέ, autem: but.
τις: a certain. Latin: quaedam.
ἐκδοχὴ: expectation. Latin: exspectātiō.
κρίσεως: of judgment, from κρίσις, whence crisis. Latin: jūdiciī, from jūdicium.
καὶ, et.
πυρὸς: of fire, from πῦρ. Latin: ignis, genitive here, though it looks nominative.
ζῆλος: zeal. Latin: aemulātiō, rivalry, zeal.

ἐσθίειν μέλλοντος: about to devour. μέλλοντος, from μέλλω, to be about to, takes the infinitive ἐσθίειν, to eat. Latin: quae cōnsūmptūra est, which is going to consume, a future participle. Its quae is feminine, so it points to zeal.
τοὺς ὑπεναντίους: the opponents. Latin: adversāriōs.

passages.en: Jesus Christ, yesterday and today, is the same, and on into the ages.

rows.note: Ἰησοῦς, Jēsūs.
Χριστὸς: Christ, the anointed one. Latin: Chrīstus.
ἐχθὲς: yesterday. Latin: herī.
καὶ, et.
σήμερον: today. Latin: hodiē.
ὁ αὐτός: the same. With the article, αὐτός means same, not he. Latin: ipse. Neither language needs a word for is.
καὶ, et.
εἰς τοὺς αἰῶνας: into the ages, that is, for ever. Latin: in saecula, from saeculum, an age.

passages.ctx: James rebukes those who boast about their plans.
passages.en: But now you boast in your arrogant ways; every boast of this kind is evil. So if someone knows how to do good and does not do it, for him it is sin.

rows.note: νῦν, nunc: now.
δὲ, autem.
καυχᾶσθε: you boast. Latin: exsultātis, you exult, from exsultō.
ἐν ταῖς ἀλαζονείαις: in the arrogant ways, from ἀλαζονεία, empty bragging. Latin also uses the plural: in superbiīs, prides.
ὑμῶν: your, literally of you. Latin uses an adjective: vestrīs.
πᾶσα: all, every. Latin: omnis.
καύχησις: boasting, from the same root as καυχᾶσθε. Latin: exsultātiō.
τοιαύτη: such, of this kind, from τοιοῦτος. Latin: tālis.
πονηρά: evil, wicked, from πονηρός. Latin: maligna, from malignus.
ἐστιν, est: is.
εἰδότι: for one knowing, a dative participle of οἶδα, to know, perfect in form, present in meaning. Latin: scientī.
οὖν: so. Latin: igitur, therefore.
καλὸν: good, from καλός, good, fine or beautiful. Latin: bonum.
ποιεῖν: to do. Latin: facere.
καὶ, et.
μὴ ποιοῦντι: not doing, another dative participle, with μή, the negative for participles. Latin: nōn facientī.
ἁμαρτία: sin. Latin: peccātum.
αὐτῷ: for him. Latin: illī.
ἐστιν, est.

passages.ctx: Peter writes to believers who are suffering.
passages.en: So then, let those too who suffer in line with God’s will commit their souls to a faithful Creator while doing good.

rows.note: ὥστε: so then. Latin: itaque.
καί, et, here meaning too.
οἱ πάσχοντες: those suffering, from πάσχω, to suffer. Latin uses a clause, hī quī patiuntur, those who suffer, from patior, passive in form, active in meaning.
κατά: according to. Latin: secundum.
τὸ θέλημα: the will, related to θέλω, to wish. Latin: voluntātem, from voluntās.
τοῦ θεοῦ: of God, Deī.
πιστῷ: faithful, from πιστός. The dative, to, agreeing with Creator. Latin: fidēlī, from fidēlis.
κτίστῃ: Creator, from κτίστης. Latin: Creātōrī, from creātor.
παρατιθέσθωσαν: let them commit, from παρατίθημι, to set before or entrust. A third person command. Latin: commendent, from commendō.
τὰς ψυχάς: the souls, animās.
αὐτῶν: their. Latin uses the reflexive suās, their own.
ἐν ἀγαθοποιΐᾳ: in doing good, from ἀγαθοποιΐα. Latin has a plural, in benefactīs, in good deeds.

passages.ctx: John writes to believers about love.
passages.en: Whoever does not love has not come to know God, since God is love.

rows.note: ὁ μὴ ἀγαπῶν: the one not loving, a participle with the article. Latin: quī nōn dīligit, who does not love.
οὐκ, nōn.
ἔγνω: knew, the aorist of γινώσκω, to know. Latin: nōvit, from nōscō. Its perfect means has come to know, and so knows.
τὸν θεόν, Deum.
ὅτι, quoniam.
ὁ θεός, Deus.
ἀγάπη: love, a noun related to ἀγαπάω. No article: it is the predicate. Latin: cāritās, from cārus, dear.
ἐστίν, est.

passages.en: Beloved, if this is how God loved us, we too are obliged to love one another.

rows.note: ἀγαπητοί: beloved, from ἀγαπητός, a vocative. Latin: cārissimī, dearest, the superlative of cārus, dear.
εἰ: if. Latin: sī.
οὕτως, sīc.
ὁ θεός, Deus.
ἠγάπησεν: loved, an aorist. Latin perfect: dīlēxit.
ἡμᾶς: us. Latin: nōs.
καί: too. Latin: et.
ἡμεῖς: we. Latin, nōs again.
ὀφείλομεν: we ought, from ὀφείλω, to owe, so ought. Latin: dēbēmus, from dēbeō, to owe.
ἀλλήλους: one another. Latin: alterutrum, from alteruter, one or the other.
ἀγαπᾶν: to love, the infinitive. Latin: dīligere.

passages.en: Fear does not exist in love, but complete love throws fear out, because fear carries punishment, and the one who fears has not been made complete in love.

rows.note: φόβος: fear. Latin: timor.
οὐκ ἔστιν: is not, nōn est.
ἐν τῇ ἀγάπῃ: in love, now in the dative after ἐν. Latin: in cāritāte, the ablative of cāritās, love.
ἀλλά: but. Latin: sed.
ἡ τελεία: complete, from τέλειος, reaching its goal. Latin: perfecta, finished, a participle of perficiō, to complete.
ἀγάπη, cāritās, now the subject.
ἔξω: out, outside, an adverb. Latin: forās, out of doors.
βάλλει: throws, from βάλλω, to throw. With ἔξω, to throw out. Latin uses mittit, sends, from mittō.
τὸν φόβον: fear, now the object. Latin: timōrem.
ὅτι, quoniam.
ὁ φόβος, timor.
κόλασιν: punishment, from κόλασις. Latin: poenam, from poena, penalty.
ἔχει: has, here carries. Latin: habet.
ὁ δὲ φοβούμενος: and the one fearing, from φοβέομαι, to fear. Latin uses a clause, quī autem timet.
οὐ, nōn.
τετελείωται: has been made complete, from τελειόω, to complete. A perfect passive: a lasting state. Latin: est perfectus, is perfected.
ἐν τῇ ἀγάπῃ, in cāritāte.

passages.en: Everyone who believes that Jesus is the Christ has been born from God, and everyone who loves the father also loves the one born from him.

rows.note: πᾶς: every, everyone. Latin: omnis.
ὁ πιστεύων: the one believing. Latin: quī crēdit, who believes.
ὅτι: that. Latin: quoniam.
Ἰησοῦς, Jēsūs.
ἐστιν, est.
ὁ χριστός: the Christ, the anointed one. Latin: Chrīstus.
ἐκ τοῦ θεοῦ: from God. Latin: ex Deō.
γεγέννηται: has been born, from γεννάω, to father, to bring to birth. A perfect passive: born, and still so. Latin: nātus est, from nāscor, to be born.
καί, et.
πᾶς, omnis.
ὁ ἀγαπῶν: the one loving, quī dīligit.
τὸν γεννήσαντα: the one who fathered, an aorist participle of γεννάω, so the father. Latin: eum quī genuit, from gignō, to beget.
ἀγαπᾷ: loves, dīligit.
καί: also, et.
τὸν γεγεννημένον: the one born, a perfect passive participle. Latin again uses a clause: eum quī nātus est.
ἐξ αὐτοῦ: from him. ἐκ becomes ἐξ before a vowel. Latin: ex eō.

nl.m: beget, father; bear, give birth to

passages.ctx: John’s vision of the beast and its mark.
passages.en: Here is the wisdom: the one who has insight should count up the number of the beast, for it is a human being’s number, and its number is six hundred sixty-six.

rows.note: ὧδε: here. Latin: hīc.
ἡ σοφία: the wisdom. Latin: sapientia.
ἐστίν, est.
ὁ ἔχων: the one having. Latin: quī habet, who has.
νοῦν: mind, insight, from νοῦς. Latin: intellēctum, from intellēctus.
ψηφισάτω: let him count, from ψηφίζω, to count with pebbles. An aorist imperative. Latin: computet, a subjunctive of command.
τὸν ἀριθμόν: the number, from ἀριθμός, behind our word arithmetic. Latin: numerum, from numerus.
τοῦ θηρίου: of the beast, from θηρίον, a wild animal. Latin: bestiae, genitive of bestia.
ἀριθμός: number, now the subject, numerus.
γάρ: for. Latin: enim.
ἀνθρώπου: of a human. Latin: hominis.
ἐστίν, est.
καί, et.
ὁ ἀριθμός, numerus.
αὐτοῦ: its. Latin: ejus.
ἑξακόσιοι: six hundred. Latin: sexcentī. Both join six and a hundred.
ἑξήκοντα ἕξ: sixty-six. Latin: sexāgintā sex. Greek ἕξ and Latin sex, six, share one ancient root.

passages.ctx: John’s vision of the thousand years.
passages.en: The others among the dead did not come alive until the thousand years were finished. This is the first resurrection.

rows.note: οἱ λοιποί: the others, the rest. Latin: cēterī.
τῶν νεκρῶν: of the dead, from νεκρός, dead. Latin: mortuōrum, from mortuus.
οὐκ, nōn.
ἔζησαν: they came alive, the aorist of ζάω, to live. Latin: vīxērunt, the perfect of vīvō.
ἄχρι: until, or as far as. Latin: dōnec.
τελεσθῇ: were finished, from τελέω, to finish. A singular verb, since the subject is neuter plural. Latin: cōnsummentur, plural.
τὰ χίλια: the thousand, from χίλιοι. Latin: mīlle, which does not change form.
ἔτη: years, the plural of ἔτος, year. Latin: annī, from annus.
αὕτη: this. Greek has no verb. Latin: haec est, this is.
ἡ ἀνάστασις: the resurrection, the rising up. Latin: resurrēctiō.
ἡ πρώτη: the first. Greek repeats the article. Latin: prīma.
